body:
Long-distance hiking trails are becoming popular
with more and more people. Let’s explore the
appeal of long-distance hiking through a famous
trail, the PCT.
The PCT, or Pacific Crest Trail, is a 4,265-kilometer
long hiking trail that stretches vertically across the
U.S. Being so long, it crosses three states and seven
national parks. Hikers can experience a varied range
of landscapes, from hot desert regions to great
mountain ranges. It takes about five months for the
average person to walk through the trail, which is
known as thru-hiking. “Thru-hikers” usually start in
early spring and head north, arriving at their
destination in early winter. It’s a hard journey with a
low completion rate; just 14% of all hikers attempting
a thru-hiking succeed in finishing the PCT.
In addition to the physical difficulties and mental
isolation, surviving in nature for months itself can
be a tremendous challenge. (A) Hikers cook their
own meals, and sometimes they have to endure
days without eating. (B) Hikers are advised to carry
the latest PCT Water Report, a list of all water
sources. (C) When it comes to sleeping, most hikers
sleep in tents, and in some areas, they can use
shelters to stay safe from the harsh weather. (D) If
you are lucky, you may find “trail angels,” who
provide transportation to close towns, meals, or
other forms of assistance. (E)
Why Do They Bother? Hear from Finishers.
• While the PCT was demanding, it was also a gift.
It allowed me to see what I am truly capable of.
• Traveling the PCT can be about the people you
meet along the way. The trail has led to lasting
friendships.
• The PCT is a journey of a lifetime. It is a chance
to see the magnificent landscapes of the
American West.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

Hobbies Create Community
J. R. R. Tolkien, the author of The Hobbit and The
Lord of the Rings, was passionate about language.
He invented languages with grammar rules and
histories: Sindarin and Quenya, the former inspired
by Welsh, and the latter inspired by Finnish and
Latin. But inventing languages was a frustrating
hobby because he had to (A)[reveal / isolate]
himself while creating them. He wrote of the
isolation that he and other people who loved
languages experienced: “But they become shy,
ashamed of spending the valuable commodity of
time for their private pleasure, and higher
developments are locked in (B)[secret / accessible]
places.”
Things are very different now. The Internet allows
people to learn about languages and meet other
language enthusiasts from all over the world.
Instead of working on their projects in (C)[private /
public], they can easily find other like-minded
people to share their passion, celebrate their
achievements, and encourage each other along the
way. They could even work together on language
projects that Tolkien may have never been able to
imagine.
(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: reveal secretprivate
isolate secretpublic
reveal accessiblepublic
isolate secretprivate
isolate accessibleprivate
solution: (A) 다음 문장에서 톨킨이 자신과 언어를 사랑하는 다른 사람 들이 겪었던 고립감(isolation)에 대해 글을 썼다고 했으므로 ‘isolate(고립시키다)’가 적절하다. (B) 앞에서, 사람들이 부끄러워하며 자신들의 사적인 즐거움을 위해 시간이라는 귀중한 재화를 쓰는 것을 부끄러워한다고 했 으므로 더 높은 수준의 언어적 발전은 결국 비밀스러운 장소 에 갇히게 된다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 ‘secret(비밀스러 운)’이 적절하다. (C) 과거에는 혼자 작업했던 것과 달리 현재는 인터넷의 발달 로 다른 이들과 소통할 수 있고, 열정을 공유할 마음이 맞는 사람들을 쉽게 찾을 수 있다고 했으므로 ‘개인적으로 자신의 프로젝트를 진행하는 대신에’라는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 ‘(in) private(개인적으로)’이 적절하다.

body:
Hobbies Can Contribute
㉠여러분은 취미를 추구하는 것이 자기만족 이상의
것을 성취할 수 있다는 사실을 알게 되어 놀랄지도 모
른다. That is, it sometimes leads to an unexpected
(A)contribution to society. For example, Thomas
Bopp, a manager at a construction materials factory
and an (B)amateur astronomer, discovered the
comet Hale-Bopp while observing the sky with his
friends in the Arizona desert. To make the story
ⓐeven more shocking, he was using a borrowed
(C)telescope that his friend had assembled himself.
And Bopp is not alone. Numerous amateur
astronomers have discovered comets, stars, and
supernovas, which helps us ⓑto better understand
the solar system and the universe. Amateurs in
many other fields have made important contributions
through their hobbies, such as amateur programmers
developing new technologies, amateur writers
publishing their work in local magazines, amateur
history researchers preserving historical sites ... The
list goes on and on!
There are many reasons why people pursue
hobbies. For many people, the challenge of learning
a new skill or achieving a difficult goal is their
primary (D)motivation. Other people enjoy hobbies
for the communities ⓒwhere they can become a
part of or the friendships they can make there. Still
others enjoy hobbies because they can lose track of
time and be in the moment, similar to being in a
(E)meditative state. Some people even end up making
contributions to society through their hobbies,
oftentimes unexpectedly. It is the physical, mental,
or emotional experience, or even a combination of
them, that makes a hobby ⓓrewarding and fun.
Perhaps it ⓔshould call “pleisure.”

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E)의 영영풀이로 알맞은 것을모두 골라 짝지은 것은?

<보기>
(A): something that you give or do in order to
help something be successful
(B): doing a job, sport, or activity for money, rather
than just for fun
(C): an optical instrument used for viewing very
small objects, such as mineral samples or
animal or plant cells
(D): the reason why you want to do something
(E): relating to the practice of emptying your
mind of thoughts and feelings, in order to
relax completely or for religious reasons
solution: (A) 공헌: 어떤 것이 성공하도록 돕기 위해 당신이 주거나 하는 것 (D) 동기: 당신이 무언가를 하고 싶어 하는 이유 (E) 명상의: 완전히 긴장을 풀기 위해 또는 종교적인 이유로 당 신의 마음에서 생각과 감정을 비워내는 수행과 관련된 비상(홍민표) 1과

(B)             (C)

solution: (A) 앞에서 PCT는 세 개의 주와 일곱 개의 국립 공원을 통과한다 고 했고, 뒤에서 뜨거운 사막 지대부터 웅장한 산맥까지 경험할 수 있다고 했으므로 다양한 풍경이라는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라 서 varied(다양한)가 적절하다. (B) 자연에서 수개월 동안 생활해야 하며 모든 수원이 마실 수 있는 것은 아니라고 했으므로, 물을 확보하는 것은 매우 중요하 다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 crucial(필수적인)이 적절하다. (C) 앞에서 낮은 완주율, 식수 확보의 어려움, 가혹한 날씨 등을 언 급했으며, ‘~이지만’을 뜻하는 접속사 While이 쓰였으므로 주절에서 언급한 ‘선물(gift)’과 대조되는 의미의 demanding(힘든)이 적절하다.

body:
Hobbies Are Modern Activities
Nowadays, everybody has a hobby they like to do
in their free time. In the past, though, this probably
wasn’t true because most people had to work long
hours in agriculture or manufacturing, so free time
must have been hard to come by. (A)____________,
the Industrial Revolution and the labor ⓐmovement
that followed it led to a gradual decrease in
working hours to eight-hour work days and five-day
work weeks. For the first time in history, a majority
of people had free time to enjoy activities that they
found meaningful outside of work: hobbies.
Hobbies Are Serious
For many people, hobbies are ⓑserious. Serious
leisure may sound like a ⓒcontradiction, but that’s
what it takes for an activity to ⓓqualify as a
hobby. To take a hobby seriously, you have to
make a meaningful effort to improve your skills,
take risks, overcome hardships, or become a better
version of yourself. If you meet someone who has
woken up at the crack of dawn to take a picture at
the “magic hour,” you can assume that they think
of themselves as a “photographer.” A runner, a
gamer, or a photographer are ⓔtitles that people
are proud to call themselves. (B)____________, you
wouldn’t call yourself a “TV watcher” or “online
surfer.” Watching TV and surfing online aren’t
considered serious hobbies because there’s no
challenge or way to improve yourself.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 알맞은 것을모두 골라 짝지은 것은?

<보기>
ⓐ movement: a change of position or place
ⓑ serious: relaxed and not worried, or seeming
not to care about something
ⓒ contradiction: a difference between two statements,
beliefs, or ideas about something
that means they cannot both be true
ⓓ qualify: to have all the necessary qualities to
be considered to be a particular thing
ⓔ title: a name that describes someone’s job or
position
solution: ⓒ 모순: 둘 다 사실일 수 없음을 의미하는 무언가에 대한 두 진술들, 믿음들, 또는 생각들 간의 차이 ⓓ 자격을 갖추다: 특정한 것으로 여겨지기 위해 필요한 모든 자질을 갖추다 ⓔ 직함: 누군가의 직업이나 지위를 설명하는 이름

You may be surprised to find that pursuing a
hobby can accomplish more than self-satisfaction.

unexpected    motivation  meditative

solution: (A) 아마추어 천문학자가 친구에게서 빌린 망원경으로 혜성을 발견한 일화를 소개하며 이를 shocking(충격적인)한 이야기라 고 표현했고, 두 번째 단락에서도 사람들이 취미를 통해 때로 는 예상치 못한 방식으로 결국 사회에 공헌하기도 한다고 했 으므로 unexpected(예상치 못한)가 적절하다. (B) 앞 문장에서 사람들이 취미를 추구하는 데는 여러 가지 이 유가 있다고 했으므로 취미를 추구하는 이유로 새로운 기술을 배우거나 어려운 목표를 달성하는 도전 과제가 흐름상 자연스 럽다. 따라서 motivation(동기)이 적절하다. (C) 빈칸 바로 앞에서 취미를 즐길 때 시간 가는 줄 모르고 그 순간에 몰입할 수 있다고 했으므로, 그것은 ‘명상하는 (meditative)’ 상태가 적절하다.

(B) 등위접속사 or에 의해, ‘A, B, C, or D’의 형태로 to에 이어 지는 동사원형들(improve, take, overcome)이 병렬 연결되어 ‘기술을 향상하고, ~ 자신이 되기 위해’라는 뜻의 부사적 용법 의 to부정사구를 이루어야 하므로 동사원형 become이 적절하 다. 또는 ‘기술을 향상하고, ~ 자신이 되기 위한 (의미 있는 노 력)’이라는 뜻으로 명사구 a meaningful effort를 수식하는 형 용사적 용법의 to부정사로 볼 수도 있다. body:
While some people pursue a hobby to improve
their skills, some do for the sheer pleasure of doing
it. Albert Einstein started learning to sail when he
was 18 years old, venturing out on the lakes in
Switzerland and simply enjoying the time on his
boat. He continued to enjoy sailing as a life-long
sailor. Although he is considered a genius in
physics, he wasn’t a good sailor, nor did he care
about his sailing technique. His technique remained
at a basic level, which was simply to “Set sail, make
it fast, no thoughts of energy or speed, lean back,
let the boat drift.”
On a boat, he forgot everything else in the world,
which may explain why he enjoyed sailing so much.
For him, it was being out on the water (A)[what /
that] mattered the most. Einstein used the hobby of
sailing to go to a place (B)[which / where] he could
be completely relaxed. Maybe that’s why he named
his boat Tinef, meaning “worthless” in Yiddish, after
the apparent meaninglessness of his sailing
adventures. (C)[Watching / Watch] the waves while
on his boat, Einstein forgot all his worries. Like
Einstein, for many people, hobbies just provide the
conditions for a sense of pure satisfaction.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: whatwhere      Watching
thatwhich      Watching
thatwhere      Watch

solution: (A) 주어 자리의 it, 동사 was와 함께 동명사구 ‘being out on the water(물 위에 나가 있는 것)’를 강조하는 ‘it is[was] ~ that …(…한 것은 바로 ~이다[이었다])’ 형태의 ‘it - that’ 강조구 문을 이루어야 하므로 that이 적절하다. (B) 완전한 절(he ~ relaxed)을 이끌어 선행사 a place를 수식하 는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 관계부사 where가 적절하다. (C) 콤마(,) 뒤의 완전한 절(Einstein ~ worries)과 접속사 없이 이어지므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며 주어 Einstein이 ‘보는’ 주체이므로 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 Watching이 적절 하다.

ⓑ            ⓒ
choices: surprised assembled  helps

body:
Long-distance hiking trails are becoming popular
with more and more people. Let’s explore the
appeal of long-distance hiking through a famous
trail, the PCT.
What Is the PCT?
The PCT, or Pacific Crest Trail, is a 4,265-kilometer
long hiking trail that stretches vertically across the
U.S. Being so long, it crosses three states and seven
national parks. Hikers can experience a varied range
of landscapes, from hot desert regions to great
mountain ranges. It takes about five months for the
average person (A)[walks / to walk] through the
trail, which is known as thru-hiking. “Thru-hikers”
usually start in early spring and head north,
(B)[arrive / arriving] at their destination in early
winter. It’s a hard journey with a low completion
rate; just 14% of all hikers attempting a thru-hiking
(C)[succeed / to succeed] in finishing the PCT.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로바르게 연결된 것은?

(A)
(B)
(C)
choices: to walk  arriveto succeed
to walk  arrivingsucceed
walks  arriveto succeed
to walk  arrivingto succeed
walks  arrivingsucceed
solution: (A) 주어 자리의 It, 동사 takes, ‘for+명사구’와 함께 ‘it takes+ 시간+for A+to부정사(구)(A가 ~하는 데 시간이 걸리다)’의 구 문을 이루어야 하므로 to부정사 to walk가 적절하다. (B) 완전한 절(“Thru-hikers” ~ north)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로 만 이어지므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어 인 “Thru-hikers”가 ‘도착하는’ 주체이자, arrive는 자동사이므로 능동의 의미인 현재분사 arriving이 적절하다. (C) 주어는 14% of all hikers이며, 이를 수식하는 분사구 attempting a thru-hiking 뒤에 이어지는 동사 자리이므로 동 사 succeed가 적절하다.

body:
J. R. R. Tolkien, the author of The Hobbit and The
Lord of the Rings, was passionate about language.
He invented languages with grammar rules and
histories: Sindarin and Quenya, the former
ⓐinspired by Welsh, and the latter inspired by
Finnish and Latin. But ⓑinventing languages was a
frustrating hobby because he had to isolate himself
while creating them. He wrote of the isolation that
he and other people who loved languages
ⓒwere experienced: “But they become shy, ashamed
of spending the valuable commodity of time for
their private pleasure, and higher developments are
locked in secret places.”
Things are very different now. The Internet allows
people ⓓto learn about languages and meet other
language enthusiasts from all over the world.
Instead of working on their projects in private, they
can easily find other like-minded people to share
their passion, ⓔcelebrate their achievements, and
encourage each other along the way. They could
even work together on language projects that
Tolkien may have never been able to imagine.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the creative skills needed to develop a completelynew language
the frustrating and lonely process of inventing anew language
the negative effects of isolating oneself
the historical background and origins of Tolkien’sinvented languages
the shift of language creation from a solitaryhobby into a shared experience

body:
다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

Nowadays, everybody has a hobby they like to do in their free time. In the past, though, this probably wasn’t true because most people had to work long hours in agriculture or manufacturing, so free time must have been hard to come by. However, the Industrial Revolution and the labor movement that followed it led to a gradual decrease in working hours to eight-hour work days and five-day work weeks. For the first time in history, a majority of people had free time to enjoy activities that they found meaningful outside of work: hobbies.

[요약문] People in the past (A)____________ time for hobbies, but (B)____________ working hours after the Industrial Revolution and the labor movement allowed them to enjoy meaningful activities beyond work.
choices: (A) wanted — (B) extended
(A) lacked — (B) extended
(A) possessed — (B) shortened
(A) lacked — (B) reduced
(A) lacked — (B) increased
solution:
1. 과거에는 대부분 농업·제조업에서 오래 일해야 해서 여가 시간을 얻기 어려웠다(free time must have been hard to come by) → (A) lacked(부족했다).
2. 산업혁명과 노동 운동 뒤 근로 시간이 하루 8시간, 주 5일로 점차 줄었다(a gradual decrease in working hours) → (B) reduced(줄어든).
3. ②·⑤는 (B)가 글과 반대이고, ①의 wanted·③의 possessed는 (A)가 글과 맞지 않는다.
4. 따라서 답은 ④이다.

While some people pursue a hobby to improve
their skills, some do for the sheer pleasure of doing
it. Albert Einstein started learning to sail when he
was 18 years old, venturing out on the lakes in
Switzerland and simply enjoying the time on his
boat. He continued to enjoy sailing as a life-long
sailor. Although he is considered a genius in
physics, he wasn’t a good sailor, nor did he care
about his sailing technique. His technique remained
at a basic level, which was simply to “Set sail, make
it fast, no thoughts of energy or speed, lean back,
let the boat drift.”
On a boat, he forgot everything else in the world,
which may explain why he enjoyed sailing so much.
For him, it was being out on the water (A)[what /
that] mattered the most. Einstein used the hobby of
sailing to go to a place (B)[which / where] he could
be completely relaxed. Maybe that’s why he named
his boat Tinef, meaning “worthless” in Yiddish, after
the apparent meaninglessness of his sailing
adventures. (C)[Watching / Watch] the waves while
on his boat, Einstein forgot all his worries. Like
Einstein, for many people, hobbies just provide the
conditions for a sense of pure satisfaction.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the common characteristics of people who pursuehigher levels of skills in hobbies
the necessity of continuous efforts to reachprofessional mastery in sailing
the value of hobbies as sources of comfort andpure enjoyment
how academic genius leads to success in physicalactivities
why highly intellectual people prefer solitaryhobbies

body:
You may be surprised to find that pursuing a
hobby can accomplish more than self-satisfaction.
That is, it sometimes leads to an unexpected
contribution to society. For example, Thomas Bopp,
a manager at a construction materials factory and
an amateur astronomer, discovered the comet
Hale-Bopp while observing the sky with his friends
in the Arizona desert. To make the story even more
shocking, he was using a borrowed telescope that
his friend had assembled himself. And Bopp is not
alone. Numerous amateur astronomers have
discovered comets, stars, and supernovas, which
helps us to better understand the solar system and
the universe. Amateurs in many other fields have
made important contributions through their hobbies,
such as amateur programmers developing new
technologies, amateur writers publishing their work
in local magazines, amateur history researchers
preserving historical sites ... The list goes on and on!

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the process of passionate amateurs becomingauthoritative professionals
the meaningful societal contributions of amateurspursuing personal hobbies
the power of simple tools in making majorscientific discoveries
the advantages of hobbies as a source of purepersonal enjoyment
popular hobbies for people seeking to changetheir career paths
solution: 아마추어 천문학자인 토마스 봅(Thomas Bopp)이 헤일-봅 혜성 을 발견한 사례와 다양한 분야의 아마추어들이 취미를 통해 사회에 기여한 사례를 제시함으로써, 취미는 개인적인 만족을 넘어 사회에도 의미 있는 기여를 할 수 있음을 보여 주고 있 으므로 이 글의 주제로 ❷ ‘개인적인 취미를 추구하는 아마추 어들의 의미 있는 사회적 기여’가 적절하다.

J. R. R. Tolkien, the author of The Hobbit and The
Lord of the Rings, was passionate about language.
He invented languages with grammar rules and
histories: Sindarin and Quenya, the former inspired
by Welsh, and the latter inspired by Finnish and
Latin. But inventing languages was a frustrating
hobby because he had to isolate himself while
creating them. He wrote of the isolation that he
and other people who loved languages experienced:
“But they become shy, ashamed of spending the
valuable commodity of time for their private
pleasure, and higher developments are locked in
secret places.”
Things are very different now. The Internet allows
people to learn about languages and meet other
language enthusiasts from all over the world.
Instead of working on their projects in private, they
can easily find other like-minded people to share
their passion, celebrate their achievements, and
encourage each other along the way. They could
even work together on language projects that
Tolkien may have never been able to imagine.

the internet now enables language enthusiasts to
find networks where they share their achievements
and collaborate
on projects

unimaginable without it.

(B)

body:
Long-distance hiking trails are becoming popular
with more and more people. Let’s explore the
appeal of long-distance hiking through a famous
trail, the PCT.
What Is the PCT?
The PCT, or Pacific Crest Trail, is a 4,265-kilometer
long hiking trail that stretches vertically across the
U.S. Being so long, it crosses three states and seven
national parks. Hikers can experience a varied range
of landscapes, from hot desert regions to great
mountain ranges. It takes about five months for the
average person (A)[walks / to walk] through the
trail, which is known as thru-hiking. “Thru-hikers”
usually start in early spring and head north,
(B)[arrive / arriving] at their destination in early
winter. It’s a hard journey with a low completion
rate; just 14% of all hikers attempting a thru-hiking
(C)[succeed / to succeed] in finishing the PCT.

다음 글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?

In addition to the physical difficulties and mental
isolation, surviving in nature for months itself can
be a tremendous challenge. Hikers cook their own
meals, and sometimes they have to endure days
without eating. Securing water is another crucial
requirement because not all the water sources are
safe to drink. Hikers are advised to carry the latest
PCT Water Report, a list of all water sources. When
it comes to sleeping, most hikers sleep in tents,
and in some areas, they can use shelters to stay
safe from the harsh weather. If you are lucky, you
may find “trail angels,” who provide transportation
to close towns, meals, or other forms of assistance.
Why Do They Bother? Hear from Finishers.
• While the PCT was demanding, it was also a gift.
It allowed me to see what I am truly capable of.
• Traveling the PCT can be about the people you
meet along the way. The trail has led to lasting
friendships.
• The PCT is a journey of a lifetime. It is a chance
to see the magnificent landscapes of the American
West.
choices: how to find safe places to sleep during long hikes
what makes hiking the PCT challenging andrewarding
unpredictable changes in weather conditions alongthe PCT
physical training required for a successfulmonths-long hike
how to overcome mental isolation and physicalhardship through extreme activities

body:
다음 글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?

For many people, hobbies are serious. Serious leisure may sound like a contradiction, but that’s what it takes for an activity to qualify as a hobby. To take a hobby seriously, you have to make a meaningful effort to improve your skills, take risks, overcome hardships, or become a better version of yourself. If you meet someone who has woken up at the crack of dawn to take a picture at the “magic hour,” you can assume that they think of themselves as a “photographer.” A runner, a gamer, or a photographer are titles that people are proud to call themselves. On the other hand, you wouldn’t call yourself a “TV watcher” or “online surfer.” Watching TV and surfing online aren’t considered serious hobbies because there’s no challenge or way to improve yourself.
choices: The Reason People Need More Free Time for Their Hobbies
Why Hobbies Can Be More Than Simple Leisure Activities
How to Balance Work and Leisure in Modern Society
Why Photography Is Considered a Rewarding Hobby
Valuable Hobbies That Can Make You an Expert

2. 도전과 발전이 없는 TV 시청·온라인 서핑은 진지한 취미로 여겨지지 않는다고 대비했다.

따라서 답은 ②이다.

Hobbies Are Gratifying
While some people pursue a hobby to improve
their skills, some do for the sheer pleasure of doing
it. Albert Einstein started learning to sail when he
was 18 years old, venturing out on the lakes in
Switzerland and simply enjoying the time on his
boat. He continued to enjoy sailing as a life-long
sailor. (A)그는 물리학의 천재로 여겨짐에도 불구하고,
뛰어난 선원이 아니었으며, 자신의 항해술에도 신경
쓰지 않았다. His technique remained at a basic
level, which was simply to “Set sail, make it fast, no
thoughts of energy or speed, lean back, let the
boat drift.”
On a boat, he forgot everything else in the world,
which may explain why he enjoyed sailing so much.
For him, it was being out on the water that
mattered the most. Einstein used the hobby of
sailing to go to a place where he could be
completely relaxed. Maybe that’s why he named his
boat Tinef, meaning “worthless” in Yiddish, after the
apparent meaninglessness of his sailing adventures.
Watching the waves while on his boat, Einstein
forgot all his worries. Like Einstein, for many people,
hobbies just provide the conditions for a sense of
pure satisfaction.

Einstein’s sailing method stayed simple rather thanbecoming highly advanced.

Sailing helped Einstein forget his concerns andrelax while he was on the water.

You may be surprised to find that pursuing a
hobby can accomplish more than self-satisfaction.
That is, it sometimes leads to an unexpected
contribution to society. For example, Thomas Bopp,
a manager at a construction materials factory and
an amateur astronomer, discovered the comet
Hale-Bopp while observing the sky with his friends
in the Arizona desert. To make the story even more
shocking, he was using a borrowed telescope that
his friend had assembled himself. And Bopp is not
alone. Numerous amateur astronomers have
discovered comets, stars, and supernovas, which
helps us to better understand the solar system and
the universe. Amateurs in many other fields have
made important contributions through their hobbies,
such as amateur programmers developing new
technologies, amateur writers publishing their work
in local magazines, amateur history researchers
preserving historical sites ... The list goes on and on!

The positive social impact of hobbies can be foundin various fields other than astronomy, includingtechnology and history.

Hobbies Are Modern Activities
Nowadays, everybody has a hobby they like to do
in their free time. In the past, though, this probably
wasn’t true because most people had to work long
hours in agriculture or manufacturing, so free time
must have been hard to come by. However, the
Industrial Revolution and the labor movement that
followed it led to a gradual decrease in working
hours to eight-hour work days and five-day work
weeks. For the first time in history, a majority of
people had free time to enjoy activities that they
found meaningful outside of work: hobbies.
Hobbies Are Serious
For many people, hobbies are serious. Serious leisure
may sound like a contradiction, but that’s what it
takes for an activity to qualify as a hobby. To take a
hobby seriously, you have to make a meaningful
effort to improve your skills, take risks, overcome
hardships, or become a better version of yourself. If
you meet someone who has woken up at the crack
of dawn to take a picture at the “magic hour,” you
can assume that they think of themselves as a
“photographer.” A runner, a gamer, or a photographer
are titles that people are proud to call themselves. On
the other hand, you wouldn’t call yourself a “TV
watcher” or “online surfer.” Watching TV and surfing
online aren’t considered serious hobbies because
there’s no challenge or way to improve yourself.

The Industrial Revolution and the labor movementcontributed to shorter working hours.

An activity can still be regarded as a serioushobby even if it offers neither challenge norpersonal development.

ⓐtransitioning to more sustainable operations before,

more responsible approaches have been made by
various organizations, and the International Olympic
Committee (IOC) is leading the way by setting a
good example. The IOC set up the Sport and
Environment Commission decades ago and ⓒdeclared
the environment as essential to the Olympic
Movement, in addition to sports and culture. It has
since encouraged host nations to adopt more
environmental approaches to putting on the Olympics.
As a result, the Olympic Village built for the 2000
Sydney Summer Olympics became the world’s
largest solar-powered suburb and the 2002 Salt
Lake City Winter Olympics ⓓadopted a new energy
recycling system which used the curling hall’s air
conditioning unit to heat the showers and bathrooms
in the ⓔvenue. Also, for the 2010 Vancouver Winter
Olympics, the Olympic speed-skating venue was built

유럽에서 가장 큰 도시 공원으로 탈바꿈되었다. Then

Every sporting event affects the environment
before, during, and even after it. For example, a
long-track speed skating competition can only take
place, provided that the ice of a 400-meter oval
track is frozen until it is 3 to 5 cm thick. As long
as the competition is on, the track needs to be
kept frozen by specialized refrigeration systems
while the temperature, humidity, and air quality
inside the stadium also have to be maintained for
optimal ice conditions. Additionally, all of the
stadium employees, athletes, and spectators need to
travel to and from the stadium, often from other
cities or even from abroad. In fact, more than 25%
of the emissions generated by the 2018
PyeongChang Winter Olympics are estimated to be
caused by fan travel and accommodations. During
the event, spectators and athletes eat and drink,
and the plastic bottles and wrappers of whatever
they consumed leave trash cans (A)[vacant /
overflowing]. After the event has ended, in addition
to the significant amount of trash that needs to be
disposed of, ⓐ그 사람들이 초래한 영향과 그들의 이
동으로부터 발생된 배기가스는 대기 질에 계속해서 지
속적인 부정적 영향을 미친다.
Alarm bells sounded when research (B)[disputed /
suggested] the possibility that nearly one in every
four English soccer stadiums could be partially or
completely flooded in the near future due to
climate change and extreme weather events. Some
research even predicted that by 2050 almost half of
the cities that once hosted the Winter Olympics
would not be able to do so again for lack of snow
and ice. Also, the US Open Tennis Championships
organizers implemented an “extreme heat policy,”
having (C)[optional / mandatory] short breaks for
players to cool down during matches, after a few
quit their matches due to extreme heat. As more
sports are affected by climate change, concerns are
growing.

Many sporting events have a negative impact on
the environment because they require massive
structures to host them. To draw more spectators,
sports stadiums and sporting facilities are getting
bigger, consuming larger areas of land and requiring
greater amounts of building materials for construction.
Whenever a hectare of grassland is cleared for a
construction site, there is a loss of nature. Every ton
of concrete and steel used in the building
foundation and structure is produced, transported,
poured, and put together by equipment and facilities
that emit waste into the ground and atmosphere.
Then, after the stadium is completed, large amounts
of water, electricity, and other forms of resources
are consumed to operate and maintain the facility.
Every sporting event affects the environment
before, during, and even after it. (A) For example, a
long-track speed skating competition can only take
place, provided that the ice of a 400-meter oval
track is frozen until it is 3 to 5 cm thick. (B) As
long as the competition is on, the track needs to
be kept frozen by specialized refrigeration systems
while the temperature, humidity, and air quality
inside the stadium also have to be maintained for
optimal ice conditions. (C) Additionally, all of the
stadium employees, athletes, and spectators need to
travel to and from the stadium, often from other
cities or even from abroad. (D) During the event,
spectators and athletes eat and drink, and the
plastic bottles and wrappers of whatever they
consumed leave trash cans overflowing. (E) After the
event has ended, in addition to the significant
amount of trash that needs to be disposed of, the
effects those people caused and the emissions
generated from their travel continue to have a
lasting negative impact on air quality.

of Mexico, causing a significant oil leak into the
sea. Over a three-month period, approximately 134
million gallons of oil, comparable to more than 200
Olympic swimming pools, flowed into the sea before
it was eventually halted. Despite continuing restoration
efforts, the sea has not yet fully recovered.
(A) When an oil spill occurs, these bacteria are
attracted to the oil and begin to multiply. As
they grow, they release enzymes that break
down oil into carbon dioxide and water.
(B) One approach to addressing the issue of oil
contamination is bioremediation, a restoration
method that utilizes bacteria. Some types of
bacteria naturally exist in marine environments
and possess the capability to break down
various components of oil.
(C) Although this process may take several weeks or
months, it represents a more sustainable method
of cleaning up oil spills compared to conventional
approaches involving harmful chemicals.
Bacteria can also play a role in the process of
plastic decomposition. When plastic enters the ocean,
some bacteria are attracted to it, leading to their
growth and reproduction. Similar to the process of
breaking down oil, the bacteria release enzymes
that break down plastic into smaller molecules,
ultimately resulting in carbon dioxide and water.

associated with bioremediation. The breakdown of
oil or plastic by bacteria, as mentioned earlier, can
be a time-consuming process requiring weeks or
months. These bacteria can also be sensitive to
specific environmental conditions such as temperature
and sea water constituents. Despite these challenges,
there is no doubt that bioremediation holds promise
as a technology for oil spill or plastic cleanup in
the ocean. Because the bacteria used in this process
occur naturally, they do not need to be transported
to the polluted site. Bioremediation may be a more
effective way to confront contamination problems
and reduce environmental harm.

including slow decomposition and bacteria's
sensitivity to environmental conditions, the use of
naturally occurring bacteria makes it a(n)
(B)______________ way to reduce pollution.

obstacles   useless

body:
Many sporting events have a negative impact on
the environment because they require massive
structures to host them. To draw more spectators,
sports stadiums and sporting facilities are getting
bigger, consuming larger areas of land and requiring
greater amounts of building materials for construction.
Whenever a hectare of grassland is cleared for a
construction site, there is a loss of nature. Every ton
of concrete and steel used in the building
foundation and structure is produced, transported,
poured, and put together by equipment and facilities
that emit waste into the ground and atmosphere.
Then, after the stadium is completed, large amounts
of water, electricity, and other forms of resources
are consumed to operate and maintain the facility.
Every sporting event affects the environment
before, during, and even after it. (A) For example, a
long-track speed skating competition can only take
place, provided that the ice of a 400-meter oval
track is frozen until it is 3 to 5 cm thick. (B) As
long as the competition is on, the track needs to
be kept frozen by specialized refrigeration systems
while the temperature, humidity, and air quality
inside the stadium also have to be maintained for
optimal ice conditions. (C) Additionally, all of the
stadium employees, athletes, and spectators need to
travel to and from the stadium, often from other
cities or even from abroad. (D) During the event,
spectators and athletes eat and drink, and the
plastic bottles and wrappers of whatever they
consumed leave trash cans overflowing. (E) After the
event has ended, in addition to the significant
amount of trash that needs to be disposed of, the
effects those people caused and the emissions
generated from their travel continue to have a
lasting negative impact on air quality.

the economic and social costs of running sportingevents

There is light at the end of the tunnel, however.
The sports community is optimistic that it can
reduce its environmental impact by taking two main
steps: transitioning to more sustainable operations
before, during, and after events and raising
awareness among the public about their impact.
Efforts to adopt more responsible approaches have
been made by various organizations, and the
International Olympic Committee (IOC) is leading
the way by setting a good example. The IOC set
up the Sport and Environment Commission decades
ago and declared the environment as essential to
the Olympic Movement, in addition to sports and
culture. It has since encouraged host nations to
adopt more environmental approaches to putting
on the Olympics.
As a result, the Olympic Village built for the 2000
Sydney Summer Olympics ⓐbecoming the world’s
largest solar-powered suburb and the 2002 Salt
Lake City Winter Olympics adopted a new energy
recycling system ⓑwhich used the curling hall’s air
conditioning unit to heat the showers and bathrooms in the venue.
Also, for the 2010
Vancouver Winter Olympics, the Olympic speed-skating
venue was built with ⓒsalvaged timber. The Olympic
Park for the 2012 London Summer Olympics,
ⓓwhat was built on industrial land that was once
contaminated, was converted to the biggest urban
park in Europe. Then at the 2020 Tokyo Summer
Olympics, electricity was ⓔgenerated with hydrogen
instead of fossil fuel, which supplied power for
many residential buildings in the Olympic Village
and Paralympic Village.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?

the role of the IOC in organizing successfulOlympic Games
the development of renewable energy technologiesfor sports facilities
the economic benefits of adopting eco-friendlyapproaches in sports
green efforts to reduce environmental impactsthrough sustainable practices

On April 20, 2010, an enormous explosion shook
the Deepwater Horizon drilling platform in the Gulf
of Mexico, causing a significant oil leak into the
sea. Over a three-month period, approximately 134
million gallons of oil, comparable to more than 200
Olympic swimming pools, flowed into the sea before
it was eventually halted. Despite continuing restoration
efforts, the sea has not yet fully recovered.
(A) When an oil spill occurs, these bacteria are
attracted to the oil and begin to multiply. As
they grow, they release enzymes that break
down oil into carbon dioxide and water.
(B) One approach to addressing the issue of oil
contamination is bioremediation, a restoration
method that utilizes bacteria. Some types of
bacteria naturally exist in marine environments
and possess the capability to break down
various components of oil.
(C) Although this process may take several weeks or
months, it represents a more sustainable method
of cleaning up oil spills compared to conventional
approaches involving harmful chemicals.
Bacteria can also play a role in the process of
plastic decomposition. When plastic enters the ocean,
some bacteria are attracted to it, leading to their
growth and reproduction. Similar to the process of
breaking down oil, the bacteria release enzymes
that break down plastic into smaller molecules,
ultimately resulting in carbon dioxide and water.

How does the carbon dioxide produced whenbacteria break down oil affect the marineenvironment?

M: Can you hand me a grocery bag?
W: Do you mean one of these cotton bags?
M: Yes. They are reusable and environmentally friendly,
unlike disposable plastic bags.
W: Are you sure? I read an article recently about
those bags. It contended that reusable bags are
only effective if they are used more than 7,100
times.
M: Is that a lot?
W: Of course. That means you’d have to utilize the
same bag every day for 20 years.
M: Wow! Then, should I give up and go back to
disposable plastic bags?
W: Not necessarily. Just remember to use reusable
bags as often as you can.
M: Okay. I’ll use the ones I have until they fall
apart.
W: Good idea. It’s important to put sustainability
into practice in our daily lives.

Thanks to its popularity, sports is a powerful tool
for universally raising awareness about
environmental responsibility. Simply put, the sports
industry influences billions of individuals that are
(A)involved in sports either as spectators, athletes,
or organizers. Through sports, strategies to increase
awareness and educate the public about the
importance of sustaining the environment (B)have
shown good results. Research has found (C)that fans
are ⓐreceptive to ecological or environmental
ⓑinitiatives organized at sporting events, and many
are willing to change their lifestyle habits accordingly.
The social status of athletes can have a strong
effect, too. For example, high-profile athletes and
coaches can be sports ⓒambassadors to foster
environmental consciousness among fans, especially
young people who look up to them. The broad
appeal of sports becomes a vehicle to reach many
people at once.
While sports provide us with such immense
benefits, we ─along with sporting event organizers
─need to be aware of the ⓓadverse environmental
effects (D)that sports have at times. As long as we
are all aware of the effects, we can take steps
toward finding ways to minimize or even completely
(E)eliminating them. While Green Sports Day, on
October 6th, is a global event that ⓔpromotes
environmentally friendly sports, maybe it’s time we
declare every day a day to encourage greater
sustainability in sports.

body:
Every sporting event affects the environment
before, during, and even after it. For example, (A)롱
트랙 스피드 스케이팅 경기는 400미터 타원형 트랙의
얼음이 그것이 3~5cm 두께가 될 때까지 얼어 있어야
만 진행될 수 있다. As long as the competition is
on, the track needs to be kept frozen by specialized refrigeration systems while the
temperature, humidity, and air quality inside the
stadium also have to be maintained for optimal ice
conditions. Additionally, all of the stadium
employees, athletes, and spectators need to travel
to and from the stadium, often from other cities or
even from abroad. In fact, more than 25% of the
emissions generated by the 2018 PyeongChang
Winter Olympics are estimated to be caused by fan
travel and accommodations. During the event,
spectators and athletes eat and drink, and the
plastic bottles and wrappers of whatever they
consumed leave trash cans overflowing. After the
event has ended, in addition to the significant
amount of trash that needs to be disposed of, the
effects those people caused and the emissions
generated from their travel continue to have a
lasting negative impact on air quality.
Alarm bells sounded when research suggested the
possibility that nearly one in every four English
soccer stadiums could be partially or completely
flooded in the near future due to climate change
and extreme weather events. Some research even
predicted that by 2050 almost half of the cities that
once hosted the Winter Olympics would not be
able to do so again for lack of snow and ice. Also,
the US Open Tennis Championships organizers
implemented an “extreme heat policy,” having
mandatory short breaks for players to cool down
during matches, after a few quit their matches due
to extreme heat. As more sports are affected by
climate change, concerns are growing.

윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Sports events affect the environment before,during, and after they take place.
Long-track speed skating competitions needspecial cooling systems and careful control ofindoor conditions.
More than 25% of the emissions from the 2018PyeongChang Winter Olympics came from fantravel and stays.
Studies predict that almost half of English soccerstadiums may be flooded by 2050 because ofclimate change.
US Open organizers created a heat policy aftersome players stopped their matches because ofextreme heat.

_________________________________, however. The sports

transitioning to more sustainable operations before,
during, and after events and raising awareness among
the public about their impact. Efforts to adopt more
responsible approaches have been made by various
organizations, and the International Olympic Committee
(IOC) is leading the way by setting a good example.
The IOC set up the Sport and Environment Commission
decades ago and declared the environment as
essential to the Olympic Movement, in addition to
sports and culture. It has since encouraged host
nations to adopt more environmental approaches to
putting on the Olympics.

body:
Many sporting events have a negative impact on
the environment because (A)_________________________
____________________________. To draw more spectators,
sports stadiums and sporting facilities are getting
bigger, consuming larger areas of land and
requiring greater amounts of building materials for
construction. Whenever a hectare of grassland is
cleared for a construction site, there is a loss of
nature. Every ton of concrete and steel used in the
building foundation and structure is produced,
transported, poured, and put together by equipment
and facilities that emit waste into the ground and
atmosphere. Then, after the stadium is completed,
large amounts of water, electricity, and other forms
of resources are consumed to operate and
ⓐ[maintain / maintained] the facility.
Every sporting event affects the environment
before, during, and even after it. For example, a
long-track speed skating competition can only take
place, provided that the ice of a 400-meter oval
track is frozen until it is 3 to 5 cm thick. As long
as the competition is on, the track needs to be
kept frozen by specialized refrigeration systems
while the temperature, humidity, and air quality
inside the stadium also have to be maintained for
optimal ice conditions. Additionally, all of the
stadium employees, athletes, and spectators need to
travel to and from the stadium, often from other
cities or even from abroad. In fact, more than 25%
of the emissions generated by the 2018
PyeongChang Winter Olympics are estimated to be
caused by fan travel and accommodations. During
the event, spectators and athletes eat and drink,
and the plastic bottles and wrappers of ⓑ[whatever
/ no matter what] they consumed leave trash cans
overflowing. After the event has ended, in addition
to the significant amount of trash that needs to be
disposed of, the effects ⓒ[that / what] those
people caused and the emissions generated from
their travel continue to have a lasting negative
impact on air quality.

dry days.

body:
Old pictures often depict people singing together in church, with their families at home or with companions at community events. Unfortunately, these scenes have become less common nowadays. There could be several reasons why singing in a group has become less common. First, we spend less time in groups these days and are more isolated. Technology has made it easier to enjoy music individually rather than in a larger setting. Instead of being played in a large setting and under social circumstances, music has become something enjoyed (A)[privately / collectively] on our personal play devices. Second, our society is more diverse, so we don’t always know the same songs. The list of music that is common to different groups of people is becoming shorter. We might also worry more about our social image, and singing in front of others can make us feel awkward. Lastly, we have (B)[less / more] entertainment options today than in the past when people gathered around the piano or the guitar just because it was fun to do so.
Although group singing has become less common, it’s an activity that can be beneficial. So why does group singing make us feel so good? Decades of research have shown that singing is good for you on many levels by reducing stress and increasing the release of happiness hormones such as endorphins, dopamine, and serotonin. Singing with others has additional benefits. It brings people closer together and helps create bonds that can support self-esteem in a more stable way. The sense of belonging and purpose created in the moment makes us feel (C)[connected to / detached from] others and to something greater. Thus, it’s no surprise that people who sing together have healthier minds and more readily participate in their communities. A few studies have reported that people who sang in choirs were more optimistic, less lonely, had stronger relationships, and were more likely to contribute positively to their communities than those who didn’t. The good news is that people can enjoy these benefits even when they’re ⓐ______. Being together is the key.

(A) 오늘날에는 사람들이 집단으로 보내는 시간이 줄고 사회적으로 고립되는 경향이 있으며, 개인용 기기로 음악을 즐기는 일이 쉬워졌다고 했으므로 음악을 ‘혼자’ 즐긴다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 privately(혼자)가 적절하다.
collectively 집단으로
(B) 과거에는 사람들이 단순히 즐거움을 위해 피아노나 기타 주변에 모였지만, 오늘날에는 집단으로 노래하는 것이 덜 흔해졌다고 했으므로, 사람들이 여가를 즐길 수 있는 다른 선택지가 ‘늘어났다’는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 more(더 많은)가 적절하다.
less 더 적은
(C) 함께 노래하는 활동은 사람들을 더 가까워지게 하고 유대감과 소속감을 형성한다고 했고, 뒤에서 함께 노래하는 사람은 자신의 지역사회에 더 적극적으로 참여한다고 했으므로, 함께 노래하는 활동을 통해 형성된 소속감과 목적의식이 우리가 다른 사람들과 또 더 큰 무언가와 연결되어 있다고 느끼게 한다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 connected to(~에 연결된)가 적절하다.
detached from ~와 동떨어진

body:
Old pictures often depict people singing together in church, with their families at home or with companions at community events. Unfortunately, these scenes have become less common nowadays. There could be several reasons why singing in a group has become less common. First, we spend less time in groups these days and are more isolated. Technology has made it easier to enjoy music individually rather than in a larger setting. Instead of being played in a large setting and under social circumstances, music has become something enjoyed (A)[privately / collectively] on our personal play devices. Second, our society is more diverse, so we don’t always know the same songs. The list of music that is common to different groups of people is becoming shorter. We might also worry more about our social image, and singing in front of others can make us feel awkward. Lastly, we have (B)[less / more] entertainment options today than in the past when people gathered around the piano or the guitar just because it was fun to do so.
Although group singing has become less common, it’s an activity that can be beneficial. So why does group singing make us feel so good? Decades of research have shown that singing is good for you on many levels by reducing stress and increasing the release of happiness hormones such as endorphins, dopamine, and serotonin. Singing with others has additional benefits. It brings people closer together and helps create bonds that can support self-esteem in a more stable way. The sense of belonging and purpose created in the moment makes us feel (C)[connected to / detached from] others and to something greater. Thus, it’s no surprise that people who sing together have healthier minds and more readily participate in their communities. A few studies have reported that people who sang in choirs were more optimistic, less lonely, had stronger relationships, and were more likely to contribute positively to their communities than those who didn’t. The good news is that people can enjoy these benefits even when they’re ⓐ______. Being together is the key.

윗글의 빈칸 ⓐ에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: watching musical performances through digital devices
competing against each other in musical contests
sharing recorded music with online communities
listening to music individually at home
singing collectively in virtual spaces
solution:
앞에서 함께 노래하는 것이 스트레스를 줄이고 유대감과 소속감을 형성하는 등 여러 긍정적인 효과를 가져온다고 설명하고, 마지막 문장에서 함께하는 것이 핵심이라고 강조하므로, 물리적으로 같은 장소에 있지 않더라도 함께 노래함으로써 이러한 이점을 얻을 수 있다는 내용이 이어져야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ⑤ ‘가상 공간에서 다른 사람들과 함께 노래하고 있는’이 적절하다.
본문변형 singing with others online → singing collectively in virtual spaces

solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓑ what → that (완전한 절(singing ~ serotonin)을 이끌어 동사 have shown의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 what을 명사절 접속사 that으로 고친다.)

ⓐ has become의 보어 자리이므로, 열등 비교급 형용사 less common은 적절하다.

ⓕ 형용사 likely(가능성이 있는)는 to부정사와 함께 쓰여 ’be more likely+to부정사(~할 가능성이 더 높다)‘을 뜻하므로 to부정사 to contribute는 적절하다.

However, the communal elements persist, manifesting their power in singing events, large and small. Singing with others can be a way to heal and help us feel connected, happy, and healthy. Maybe it is in our genes as a (C)[social / solitary] species. Just open your mouth, start making a sound, and let your voice go. You’ll know how good it is almost instantly.

choices: integrated / personal / social
isolated / personal / social
integrated / collective / solitary

isolated / personal / solitary
solution:

integrated 통합된

(C) 다른 사람들과 함께 노래하는 것이 우리를 치유하고 서로 연결되어 있다고 느끼게 하며 행복과 건강에도 도움을 준다고 했으므로, 이러한 특성이 사회적 존재인 인간의 본성에 내재되어 있을 수 있다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 social(사회적인)이 적절하다.

Old pictures often depict people singing together in church, with their families at home or with companions at community events. Unfortunately, these scenes have become less common nowadays. There could be several reasons why singing in a group has become less common. First, we spend less time in groups these days and are more isolated. Technology has made it easier to ______. Instead of being played in a large setting and under social circumstances, music has become something enjoyed privately on our personal play devices. Second, our society is more diverse, so we don’t always know the same songs. The list of music that is common to different groups of people is becoming shorter. We might also worry more about our social image, and singing in front of others can make us feel awkward. Lastly, we have more entertainment options today than in the past when people gathered around the piano or the guitar just because it was fun to do so.
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: discover new songs through various musical platforms
seek opportunities to enjoy music together with others
become familiar with music from different cultures
participate in musical activities with larger groups
listen to music alone rather than with others
solution:

Although group singing has become less common, it’s an activity that can be beneficial. So why does group singing make us feel so good? Decades of research have shown ⓐthat singing is good for you on many levels by reducing stress and increasing the release of happiness hormones such as endorphins, dopamine, and serotonin. Singing with others ⓑhave additional benefits. It brings people closer together and helps create bonds that can support self-esteem in a more stable way. The sense of belonging and purpose ⓒcreated in the moment makes us feel connected to others and to something greater. Thus, it’s no surprise ⓓwhich people who sing together have healthier minds and more readily participate in their communities. A few studies have reported that people who sang in choirs were more optimistic, less lonely, had stronger relationships, and ⓔwere more likely to contribute positively to their communities than those who didn’t. The good news is that people can enjoy these benefits even when they’re singing with others online. Being together is the key.

Group singing provides emotional benefits through lowered ______ and the release of more ______ hormones while supporting ______ by fostering social bonds and helping people feel ______ to others and contribute positively to their ______.
solution: [요약문] 집단으로 노래 부르는 것은 낮아진 스트레스와 더 많은 행복 호르몬의 분비를 통해 정서적 이점을 제공하는 동시에, 사회적 유대감을 형성하여 자존감을 뒷받침하고 사람들이 타인과 연결되어 있다고 느끼며 공동체에 긍정적으로 기여하도록 돕는다.

The communal nature of music remains and is vividly demonstrated at live concerts. Whether you’re in the crowd at the Mercury Lounge or Madison Square Garden, the point is ⓐ[gather / to gather] with people who love what you love. If the point wasn’t to gather or to share in the mass performance, you’d just stay home and listen to music by yourself. (A) When you sing along to songs at a concert, you don’t just listen to the music; you participate in it, “ⓑ[completing / complete]” the musical experience. (B) This creates a sense of belonging and a strong bond with the musician. (C) Many musicians remember the first time their audience sang along with them. (D) Maybe it means they have reached the point in their career ⓒ[which / where] they have become popular. (E)
윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
Even singers with long, successful careers feel energized by the power of the crowd and get inspired for their next music project.
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘오랜 성공적인 경력을 가진 가수들조차도 관중의 힘에서 활력을 얻으며 다음 음악 프로젝트에 대한 영감을 받는다.’라는 뜻으로, Even을 통해 이 문장 앞에는 일반적인 음악가들이 관객의 힘을 통해 얻는 경험이나 영향에 관한 내용이 제시되어야 함을 알 수 있다. 따라서 (D) 앞에서 많은 음악가들(Many musicians)이 관객이 처음으로 함께 노래한 순간을 기억한다고 했고, (E) 앞에서는 이 음악가들을 They(그들)로 이어받아, 그 순간이 음악가로서 대중적인 인기를 얻었음을 의미할 수 있다고 설명한다. 그리고 주어진 문장은 이러한 음악가들에 이어 오랜 성공적인 경력을 쌓은 가수들조차 관중에게서 활력과 영감을 얻는다는 내용을 덧붙이므로 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은 (E)이다.

Old pictures often depict people singing together in church, with their families at home or with companions at community events. Unfortunately, these scenes have become less common nowadays. There could be several reasons why singing in a group has become less common. First, we spend less time in groups these days and are more isolated. Technology has made it easier to enjoy music individually rather than in a larger setting. Instead of being played in a large setting and under social circumstances, music has become something enjoyed privately on our personal play devices. Second, our society is more diverse, so we don’t always know the same songs. The list of music that ______ is becoming shorter. We might also worry more about our social image, and singing in front of others can make us feel awkward. Lastly, we have more entertainment options today than in the past when people gathered around the piano or the guitar just because it was fun to do so.
윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the evolving ways people discover and share music
the changing role of music in shaping social relationships
the growing impact of personal music devices on musical tastes
the influence of social values on people's musical preferences
social changes behind the decline of group singing in modern life

body:
Although group singing has become less common, it’s an activity that can be beneficial. So why does group singing make us feel so good? Decades of research have shown that singing is good for you on many levels by reducing stress and increasing the release of happiness hormones such as endorphins, dopamine, and serotonin. Singing with others has additional benefits. It brings people closer together and helps create bonds that can support self-esteem in a more stable way. The sense of belonging and purpose created in the moment makes us feel connected to others and to something greater. Thus, it’s no surprise that people who sing together have healthier minds and more readily participate in their communities. A few studies have reported that people who sang in choirs were more optimistic, less lonely, had stronger relationships, and were more likely to contribute positively to their communities than those who didn’t. The good news is that people can enjoy these benefits even when they’re singing with others online. Being together is the key.
다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?
choices: Why has group singing become less common nowadays?
What effects does singing have on stress and mood?
What additional benefits can people gain from singing with others?
How can singing together contribute to people's self-esteem?
What differences were found between people who sang in choirs and those who did not?

body:
In a highly connected world ⓐwhere technology doesn’t necessarily connect people in a human way, individuals become socially ⓑisolated and feel intense loneliness. The invention of portable music players and earphones has made music more personal, too. However, the communal elements persist, manifesting their power in singing events, large and small. Singing with others can be a way to heal and help us ⓒfeel connected, happy, and healthy. Maybe it is in our genes as a social species. Just open your mouth, start making a sound, and let your voice ⓓgo. You’ll know how good it is almost ⓔinstant.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓔ instant → instantly (부사 almost의 수식을 받으며, 동시에 동사 know를 수식하므로 형용사 instant를 부사 instantly로 고친다.
참고로 know의 목적어는 how ~ is까지의 간접의문문이므로 is의 보어가 아님에 주의한다.)
오답
ⓐ 완전한 절(technology ~ way)을 이끌어 장소를 뜻하는 명사구 a highly connected world를 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절을 이루고 있으므로 관계부사 where는 적절하다.
ⓑ 2형식 동사 become에 이어지는 보어 자리이며, 주어 individuals가 ‘고립된’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 가진 과거분사 형태의 형용사 isolated는 적절하다.
ⓒ 동사 help와 목적어인 us 뒤에 이어진 목적격보어 자리이며, 'help+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하는 것을 돕다)'의 5형식 구문에서 동사 help는 목적격보어로 동사원형 또는 to부정사를 취하므로 동사원형 feel은 적절하다.
ⓓ ‘~가 …하게 하다’라는 뜻의 사역동사 let은 ‘let+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형)’의 구조로, let은 목적격보어로 동사원형을 취하므로 동사원형 go는 적절하다.

ⓔ 진주어 to do so에 상응하는 가주어 자리이므로 주어 자리의 it은 적절하다.

윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?

solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘다른 사람들과 함께 노래하는 것에는 추가적인 이점이 있다.’라는 뜻으로, 이 문장 앞에는 다른 사람들과 함께 노래하기와 관련된 이점이 제시되고 이 문장 뒤에는 다른 사람들과 함께 노래하기의 또 다른 이점이 이어져야 한다. body:
The ⓐindividual nature of music remains and is vividly demonstrated at live concerts. Whether you’re in the crowd at the Mercury Lounge or Madison Square Garden, the point is to gather with people who love (A)[that / what] you love. If the point wasn’t to gather or to share in the mass performance, you’d just (B)[stay / have stayed] home and listen to music by yourself. When you sing along to songs at a concert, you don’t just listen to the music; you ⓑparticipate in it, “completing” the musical experience. This creates a sense of ⓒbelonging and a strong bond with the musician. Many musicians remember the first time their audience sang along with them. body:
Although group singing has become less common, it’s an activity that can be beneficial. So why does group singing make us feel so good? Decades of research have shown that singing is good for you on many levels by reducing stress and increasing the release of happiness hormones such as endorphins, dopamine, and serotonin. Singing with others has additional benefits. It brings people closer together and helps create bonds that can support self-esteem in a more stable way. (A)그 순간에 형성되는 소속감과 목적의식은 우리가 다른 사람들과 또 더 큰 무언가와 연결되어 있다고 느끼게 만든다. Thus, it’s no surprise that people who sing together have healthier minds and more readily participate in their communities. A few studies have reported that people who sang in choirs were more optimistic, less lonely, had stronger relationships, and were more likely to contribute positively to their communities than those who didn’t. The good news is that people can enjoy these benefits even when they’re singing with others online. Being together is the key.
윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: According to research, singing reduces stress and increases the release of happiness-related hormones.
Singing with others can help people build closer relationships and maintain a more stable sense of self-worth.
People who sing in choirs tend to have stronger relationships and a more positive outlook.
Choir singers were more likely to make a positive contribution to their communities.
The benefits of group singing depend on everyone being physically present in the same place.

W: Logan, how was your weekend? Did you do anything special?
M: It was good. I went to the city homeless shelter as usual.
W: (A)Are you saying that you visit there regularly?
M: Yeah. I volunteer there every Saturday, serving meals to people at the shelter.
W: That’s amazing. It must be rewarding.

M: Interesting… So rather than just helping others when I volunteer, it sounds like I’m benefiting a lot, too.
W: Kindness makes a world of difference!

Her classmates start noticing her mood, and some are even laughing at her stomach noises. Embarrassed and angry, she snaps at her friends. Have you ever felt like Jenny?
A New English Word
After eating a delicious meal, we feel full, happy, and relaxed. That doesn’t occur when we are hungry; hunger causes ⓒdiscomfort and weakness and often sparks negative emotions. “You’re not you when you’re hungry,” was a famous candy bar commercial slogan a few years ago. What this slogan means is hunger can seriously ⓓchange your mood and performance. The phenomenon of getting annoyed and irritated due to hunger is so ⓔunusual that the word “hangry,” a combination of hungry and angry, has become an official English word in many international dictionaries. body:
Hunger and Psychology
The word hangry caught the attention of psychologists, so researchers conducted a series of experiments with over two hundred U.S. college students. Participants were asked to either skip eating or eat a big meal right before the experiment. Their performance and behavior at varying levels of difficulty in tasks involving selective attention, mental rotation, writing, and frustration management were recorded and analyzed. The results showed that participants who skipped eating had poorer performance than those who ate beforehand. Some people seem to have a deep dislike of certain foods like cucumbers. Did you know that this may be due to genetics rather than preference? Cucumbers and other similar plants produce a bitter substance around the stem, which seems to protect the plant against bugs and animals. Researchers have discovered that there is a particular gene that makes some people very sensitive to the taste of bitterness, while others are less bothered by it. ⓐ______, other foods like watermelon, sweet melon, or even cilantro might get the thumbs down from people sensitive to the gene, too! So you can blame your genes if you don’t like those foods.
But wait, there’s more! Some individuals have an issue with the smell of cucumbers in addition to the bitter taste. Genes influence the way we smell things in general, and some people are sensitive to chemical compounds that are key to the cucumber smell. Our sense of smell is as unique as we are, with over 400 types of smell receptors, creating plentiful variations. While scientists are currently searching for the precise receptors linked to the cucumber scent, some genes might make certain individuals more sensitive to those compounds. ⓑ______, some people may detect a soap- or lotion-like scent from cilantro due to the chemical compounds it contains.
We all seem to be wired differently when it comes to taste preferences. More than just a matter of whether you like or dislike something, it could come from something deep within our DNA. Thus, maybe it’s not appropriate to give people a hard time for disliking certain foods. Let’s celebrate the fact that we are all different and share a plate of understanding.

body:
The word hangry caught the attention of psychologists, so researchers conducted a series of experiments with over two hundred U.S. college students. Participants were asked to either skip eating or eat a big meal right before the experiment. Their performance and behavior at varying levels of difficulty in tasks involving selective attention, mental rotation, writing, and frustration management were recorded and analyzed. The results showed that participants who skipped eating had poorer performance than those who ate beforehand. For example, they made more errors on the Stroop task, in ⓐ[that / which] the participants were shown a color name printed in a different colored ink, and they were asked to say either the word or the color of the ink. Consequently, psychological studies seem to suggest that an empty stomach contributes to lower attention span and self-control.
Psychology is not the only field of science concerned with the relation between hunger and anger; physiologists know ⓑ[what / that] hunger leads to changes in body reactions, too. When we eat bread, rice, or fruit, our digestive system breaks these foods down into glucose, the main fuel source for the cells in our body. It circulates in the blood and gets absorbed by cells for the energy required for their proper performance. But glucose levels fall when we are hungry, preventing cells from performing what they are supposed ⓒ[to do / to be done], an obvious threat to the proper functioning of the body. The human body responds to this threat by releasing cortisol, a hormone that helps our body cope with stressful situations. Elevated cortisol levels lead to an increase in heart rate and blood pressure along with many psychological effects including anxiety, irritation, and depression. These physiological reactions seem to be in (A)[line / conflict] with psychological studies.
What is also affected by an empty stomach is the brain. Neurologists have found that (B)[low / high] levels of cortisol cause the serotonin level in the brain to drop. Serotonin is a neurotransmitter that helps communication among neurons in different parts of the brain. Neurotransmitters play a crucial role in ㉠______. When serotonin levels are not balanced, normal functioning of mood regulation is disrupted, which can lead to feelings of sadness, increased irritability, and higher levels of anxiety. Neurologists have also come across interesting findings related to hunger and mental state by using brain imaging techniques to take pictures of brain activity. These images clearly show that, when people are hungry, areas related to threat and negative emotions increase in activity, while the activity patterns in areas responsible for higher cognitive skills like self-control and decision-making are greatly (C)[altered / stabilized]. Psychology, physiology, and neurology seem to agree that “You’re not you when you’re hungry.”

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A)    (B)    (C)
choices: line    low    altered
line    high    stabilized
conflict    low    stabilized
line    high    altered
conflict    high    altered
solution:
(A) 앞 문단의 심리학 연구 결과로 배고픔이 주의 지속 기간과 자기 통제력 저하를 불러왔듯이, 생리학적으로도 배고픔이 코르티솔을 증가시켜 불안, 짜증, 우울감 같은 현상과 심박수 혈압 상승으로 이어지는 등 부정적으로 이어지므로 두 연구 결과 ‘일치한다’는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 ‘~와 일치하여, ~에 부합하여‘의 의미를 갖는 in line with의 line이 알맞다.
in conflict with ~ ~와 충돌하여, ~와 상충하여
(B) 앞 문단에서 포도당 수치가 떨어지면 코르티솔이 분비되어 코르티솔 수치가 높아진다고 했으므로, 공복에 대한 영향으로 ‘높은’ 코르티솔의 수치가 세로토닌을 떨어뜨린다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 high(높은)가 적절하다.
low 낮은
(C) 첫 문장에서 공복이 뇌에 영향을 미친다고 했고, 마지막에는 배고플 때 평소와 달라진다는 점을 강조하므로, 고차원적 인지 기능을 담당하는 영역의 활동 양식이 크게 ‘달라진다’는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 altered(바뀌게 된)가 적절하다.
stabilize 안정화시키다

body:
While being hangry refers to the emotional feelings of anger caused by the physical needs of the body, a phenomenon called “lonely hunger” works the other way around, namely from the feelings of loneliness to the need for physical nourishment. That is, some people feel hungry when they feel lonely and isolated from others, often looking for comfort in excessive “emotional eating.” Emotional eating may be a good way to relieve negative emotions in the short term, but it is not necessarily a good long-term solution due to health risks.
Interestingly, the human brain’s response to loneliness is similar to its response to hunger, as brain imaging studies have shown that the same area in the brain is turned on when a person has these feelings. Studies also support the notion that loneliness serves as a signal similar to hunger, indicating a lack that needs to be addressed. Just as a lack of physical nourishment leads to psychological discomfort, a lack of social nourishment results in feelings of social hunger, a deficit that needs to be addressed.

다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 지문에서 찾아 한 단어로 각각 쓰시오.
“______ ______" is a phenomenon in which feelings of loneliness, associated with activity in the ______ brain area as physical hunger, drive people toward ______ ______ because of a lack of ______ ______, even though this coping method carries long-term health risks.
answer: Lonely hunger, same, emotional eating, social nourishment

W: Hey, Jake! What do you plan on doing for dinner tonight?
M: I’ll probably just go get a hamburger and fries.
W: Again? You have that all the time.
M: Yeah... It’s quick and easy to get.
W: Why don’t you come to my house for dinner instead? It’ll be healthier. And you won’t have to eat alone.
M: Oh! That sounds fun.
W: Some of my other friends are coming over, too. I’m going to cook.
M: Cool! I’m in! What are you going to make?
W: I’m making a South American rice dish. I need to stop at the grocery store on the way home to get some ingredients. I’ve never made the dish before, so I hope it turns out well.
M: Sounds delicious. Thanks for inviting me.
W: You’re more than welcome. I think you’ll like it more than a fast-food burger.
다음 대화의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Jake usually has hamburgers and fries because they are convenient to get.
The woman invites Jake to have dinner at her house instead of eating fast food.
The woman is going to cook for some friends of hers.
The woman has cooked the South American rice dish many times before.
Jake accepts the invitation and the woman thinks he will like her food.

body:
After eating a delicious meal, we feel full, happy, and relaxed. That doesn’t occur when we are hungry; hunger causes discomfort and weakness and often sparks negative emotions. “You’re not you when you’re hungry,” was a famous candy bar commercial slogan a few years ago. What this slogan means is hunger can seriously change your mood and performance. The phenomenon of getting annoyed and irritated due to hunger is so common that the word “hangry,” a combination of hungry and angry, has become an official English word in many international dictionaries. So how does it work?
윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Having a delicious meal can make people feel comfortable and happy.
Hunger often brings physical weakness and negative feelings.
A well-known candy bar used the slogan “You’re not you when you’re hungry” in its ads a few years ago.
The slogan shows that hunger can affect both a person's emotional state and their overall performance.
Getting annoyed because of hunger is too rare for the word “hangry” to be officially added to dictionaries.
solution:
배고픔으로 인해 짜증이 나고 예민해지는 현상은 너무 흔해서 ’hangry‘라는 단어가 사전에 실렸다고 했으므로 ⑤ ‘배고픔으로 인해 짜증이 나는 것은 너무 드물어, 'hangry'라는 단어가 공식적으로 사전에 추가될 수 없다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
오답
① 맛있는 식사를 하는 것은 사람들이 편안하고 행복하게 느끼도록 만들 수 있다.
② 배고픔은 종종 신체적인 쇠약과 부정적인 감정들을 가져온다.
③ 한 유명한 초코 바는 몇 년 전 광고에서 “배고플 땐 너답지 않아.”라는 문구를 사용했다.
④ 그 문구는 배고픔은 한 사람의 감정 상태와 전반적인 수행 능력 모두에 영향을 미칠 수 있음을 보여 준다.

Hunger and Hormones
Psychology is not the only field of science concerned with the relation between hunger and anger; physiologists know ⓐthat hunger leads to changes in body reactions, too. When we eat bread, rice, or fruit, our digestive system breaks these foods down into glucose, the main fuel source for the cells in our body. It circulates in the blood and gets ⓑabsorbed by cells for the energy required for their proper performance. But glucose levels fall when we are hungry, preventing cells from performing ⓒthat they are supposed to do, an obvious threat to the proper functioning of the body. The human body responds to this threat by releasing cortisol, a hormone that helps our body ⓓcope with stressful situations. Elevated cortisol levels lead to an increase in heart rate and blood pressure along with many psychological effects ⓔincluding anxiety, irritation, and depression. These physiological reactions seem to be in line with psychological studies.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓒ that → what (to do의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(they ~ do)을 이끌어 선행사 없이 동명사 performing의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로, that을 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 what으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ 완전한 절(hunger ~ too)을 이끌어 동사 know의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루고 있으므로 명사절 접속사 that은 적절하다.
ⓑ 동사 gets의 보어 자리이며, 주어 It(=glucose)이 ‘흡수되는’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 absorbed는 적절하다.
ⓓ 주격 관계대명사 that이 이끄는 절의 동사 helps는 준사역동사로 ‘help+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형/to부정사)’의 구조로 쓰여 목적격보어로 항상 동사원형 또는 to부정사를 취하므로, 목적격보어로 동사원형 cope이 쓰인 것은 적절하다.
ⓔ ‘~를 포함하여’의 의미로 구체적 예시(anxiety, irritation, and depression)를 나타내는 명사구를 이끌어 앞의 명사구 many psychological effects를 수식할 수 있는 전치사 including은 적절하다.

body:
You Are in Control
Does this mean that everyone who is hungry gets irritated about something? No. Individuals vary in their genes and personality as well as in their lifestyle and experiences, so their physiological or neurological reactions to hunger can vary as well. In fact, scientists have observed that the behavior of many animals is closely linked to the availability of nourishment, too. (A)______, fruit flies get more aggressive when deprived of food, and schooling fish exhibit reduced group unity when hungry. Regardless, there is another interesting finding from the research of psychologists on hunger: People seem to be able to control their negative emotions, but only if they are able to recognize them. If you happen to find yourself angry, take a few deep breaths and ask yourself if you skipped lunch. What might be happening is you’re just hangry.
Loneliness and Hunger
While being hangry refers to the emotional feelings of anger caused by the physical needs of the body, a phenomenon called “lonely hunger” works the other way around, namely from the feelings of loneliness to the need for physical nourishment. (B)______, some people feel hungry when they feel lonely and isolated from others, often looking for comfort in excessive “emotional eating.” Emotional eating may be a good way to relieve negative emotions in the short term, but it is not necessarily a good long-term solution due to health risks.

body:
Hunger and Psychology
The word hangry caught the attention of psychologists, so researchers conducted a series of experiments with over two hundred U.S. college students. (A) Participants were asked to either skip eating or eat a big meal right before the experiment. (B) Their performance and behavior at varying levels of difficulty in tasks involving selective attention, mental rotation, writing, and frustration management were recorded and analyzed. (C) For example, they made more errors on the Stroop task, in which the participants were shown a color name printed in a different colored ink, and they were asked to say either the word or the color of the ink. (D) Consequently, psychological studies seem to suggest that an empty stomach contributes to lower attention span and self-control. (E)
The results showed that participants who skipped eating had poorer performance than those who ate beforehand.
윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘그 결과는 식사를 거른 참가자들이 미리 식사를 했던 참가자들보다 수행 능력이 더 낮았다는 사실을 보여 주었다.’라는 의미로, 앞에는 두 유형의 참가자들과 관련된 실험 내용과 과정 등이 언급되어야 한다. (A) 뒤에서 참가자들의 두 가지 다른 유형을 설명하고 있고, (B) 뒤에서는 다양한 과제에서 참가자들의 수행과 행동을 기록하고 분석했다고 설명했다고 언급하고 있으므로, 그 기록과 분석의 결과를 주어진 문장의 The result가 가리키고 있으므로 주어진 문장은 (C) 이후에 들어가는 것이 자연스러우며, 뒤에 For example(예를 들어)로 시작하여, 주어진 문장에서 언급한 ‘poorer performance’의 구체적인 예로 식사를 거른 참가자들이 Stroop 과제에서 더 많은 실수를 했다는 내용이 이어지므로, 주어진 문장은 실험 결과를 기록하고 분석했다는 내용과 구체적인 사례 사이인 (C)에 들어가야 한다.

body:
Some people seem to have a deep dislike of certain foods like cucumbers. Did you know that this may be due to genetics rather than preference? Cucumbers and other similar plants produce a bitter substance around the stem, which seems to protect the plant against bugs and animals. Researchers have discovered that there is a particular gene that makes some people very sensitive to the taste of bitterness, while others are less bothered by it. Moreover, other foods like watermelon, sweet melon, or even cilantro might get the thumbs down from people sensitive to the gene, too! So you can blame your (A)[genes / environment] if you don’t like those foods.
But wait, there’s more! Some individuals have an issue with the smell of cucumbers in addition to the bitter taste. Genes influence the way we smell things in general, and some people are sensitive to chemical compounds that are key to the cucumber smell. Our sense of smell is as (B)[common / unique] as we are, with over 400 types of smell receptors, creating plentiful variations. While scientists are currently searching for the precise receptors linked to the cucumber scent, some genes might make certain individuals more sensitive to those compounds. For example, some people may detect a soap- or lotion-like scent from cilantro due to the chemical compounds it contains.
We all seem to be wired (C)[similarly / differently] when it comes to taste preferences. More than just a matter of whether you like or dislike something, it could come from something deep within our DNA. Thus, maybe it’s not appropriate to give people a hard time for disliking certain foods. Let’s celebrate the fact that we are all different and share a plate of understanding.
다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: environment / unique / differently
genes / unique / similarly
genes / common / differently
environment / common / similarly
genes / unique / differently
solution:
(A) 오이와 같이 특정 음식에 대한 강한 혐오감이 기호보다는 유전일 수 있으며, 오이가 생성하는 쓴맛의 물질을 매우 민감하게 느끼는 특정 유전자가 있다는 사실을 밝혀냈다는 내용이 언급되었으므로, 그러므로 어떤 음식을 싫어한다면 자신의 ‘유전자’를 탓할 수 있다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 genes(유전자)가 적절하다.
environment 환경
(B) 뒤에서 400가지가 넘는 후각 수용체가 존재하여 다양성을 만들어낸다고 했으므로, 후각은 우리 자신만큼이나 ‘독특하다’는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 unique(독특한)가 적절하다.
common 흔한
(C) 특정 음식을 싫어하는 원인이 유전자와 타고난 후각 수용체에 따라 다를 수 있다는 내용이 이어지고 있으므로, 음식 취향에 있어서 우리 모두 타고나게 ‘다른’ 것처럼 보인다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 differently(다르게)가 적절하다.
