body:
Loneliness and Hunger
While being hangry ⓐrefers to the emotional feelings of anger caused by the physical needs of the body, a phenomenon called “lonely hunger” works ⓑthe other way around, namely from the feelings of loneliness to the need for physical ⓒnourishment. That is, some people feel hungry when they feel lonely and isolated from others, often looking for comfort in ⓓexcessive “emotional eating.” Emotional eating may be a good way to relieve negative emotions in the short term, but it is not necessarily a good long-term solution due to health risks.
Interestingly, the human brain’s response to loneliness is similar to its response to hunger, as brain imaging studies have shown that the same area in the brain is turned on when a person has these feelings. (A)연구는 또한 외로움이 배고픔과 비슷한 신호로 작용한다는 견해를 지지하는데, 이는 해결될 필요가 있는 결핍 상태를 나타낸다는 것이다. Just as a lack of physical nourishment leads to psychological discomfort, a lack of social nourishment results in feelings of social hunger, a deficit that needs to be ⓔaddressed.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 알맞은 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
<보기>
ⓐ refer to: to mention or speak about somebody or something
ⓑ the other way around: the opposite of what you have just mentioned
ⓒ nourishment: the food and other substances that people and other living things need to live, grow, and stay healthy
ⓓ excessive: even less than is reasonable or necessary
ⓔ address: to say something directly to somebody

A New English Word
After eating a delicious meal, we feel full, happy, and relaxed. That doesn’t occur when we are hungry; hunger causes discomfort and weakness and often sparks negative emotions. “You’re not you when you’re hungry,” was a famous candy bar commercial slogan a few years ago. What this slogan means is ______. The phenomenon of getting annoyed and irritated due to hunger is so common that the word “hangry,” a combination of hungry and angry, has become an official English word in many international dictionaries. So how does it work?
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: what feels like hunger is not always genuine hunger
you can feel hungry when losing your sense of identity
hunger can seriously change your mood and behavior
eating a lot of food can often shows your real personality
people tend to make better decisions when they are hungry

W: Dad, can you help me? I’m working on a history report, and I’m having trouble verifying the data.
M: What kind of data are you having trouble with?
W: I’m trying to figure out how many people died in the Civil War. I’ve found a few different sources, but they all give different numbers.
M: In my opinion, sources like the National History Society will give more accurate data.
W: That’s a good point. I’ll search online for those types of sources.
M: And make sure you don’t depend on one single source. Sometimes government websites give different numbers on the same topic.
W: Okay. I’ll keep that in mind.

choices: The daughter is currently struggling to confirm the credibility of historical information for her project.
Various historical sources provided conflicting figures regarding the number of people killed in the Civil War.
The father believes that sources like the National History Society provide more accurate historical data.
The father claims that government websites generally provide the same figures on historical events.
The daughter accepts her father's advice about using more than one source.

body:
[1]
Vertical reading involves relying on the text to determine the ⓐreliability or validity of information. In school, students learn to examine an author’s credibility, their logic, and their ⓑreferences based on only their text. (A)[Being read / Having read] a book, for example, a reader can review if the arguments presented in the text are supported by enough evidence, look at who the author or the publisher is, or check the references cited in the text. However, technology has changed the ⓒlandscape in which people write and publish, making (B)[it / them] necessary to change reading strategies.
[2]
Vertical reading is still useful, but new strategies must be adopted to ⓓnavigate the vast online world. One of these strategies is called “lateral reading,” which involves verifying information while reading by checking as many sources as you can. This is useful because only one source is not enough. Checking information from multiple sources with various types of content, such as text, images, and videos, is helpful to verify something you have read and gain insight.
For example, suppose a student reads an article on a popular online news site about the health of a population of people. Having come across some statistics about the number of people who are hospitalized due to poor diet, she can employ the lateral reading strategy by simply opening up another tab in her browser and accessing different sources to verify the numbers. In fact, she can open up as many new tabs as she wants to verify any type of information that (C)[is being / being] presented, such as statistics in charts and tables, or general ⓔassertions. She can look up information from other popular news sites or go directly to a scientific journal article to read from the primary source of information.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 영영풀이로 알맞은 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
<보기>
ⓐ reliability: the state of depending on or trusting in something or someone
ⓑ reference: a book, article, etc. from which information has been obtained
ⓒ landscape: a picture showing an area of countryside or land
ⓓ navigate: to find your way around on a particular website, or to move from one website to another
ⓔ assertion: something that you say or write that you strongly believe
solution: 정답은 ⑤ 이다. (해설 없음)

solution:
(A) 완전한 절(a reader ~ the text) 앞에 콤마로만 연결되어 있으므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 문맥상 주절의 내용인 독자가 검토하거나, 살펴보거나, 화인하는 것보다 책을 읽는 것이 더 먼저 일어난 일이며, 의미상 주어인 a reader가 책을 ‘읽는’ 주체이므로 완료분사구문의 능동태(having p.p.)로 써야 한다. 따라서 Having read가 적절하다.
(B) 분사구문을 이루는 현재분사 making의 목적어 자리이며 ‘make+가목적어+목적격보어+for+의미상주어+진목적어(to부정사)(~하는 것을 …하게 만들다)’ 형태의 5형식 구문을 이루고 있으므로 진목적어인 to부정사에 상응하는 가목적어 역할을 하는 it이 적절하다.
(C) 주격 관계대명사 that이 이끄는 주격 관계대명사절의 동사구를 이루는 자리로, 선행사 any type of information은 단수명사구이며 ‘제시되고 있는’ 대상이므로 뒤의 과거분사 presented와 함께 진행수동태(be being p.p.)를 이루는 is being이 적절하다.

Vertical reading is not a perfect strategy and neither is lateral reading, but lateral reading takes greater advantage of modern technology than vertical reading. To fully appreciate this strategy, a reader in the digital world makes evaluating all forms of information a habit. No matter how neutral an author or publication claims to be, the burden of evaluation falls upon the reader to survey as much information as possible to determine the credibility of the data or the claims. We need to understand that the world, and therefore information itself, is constantly evolving: information does not remain still, so neither should the reader. For this reason, ______. Instead of approaching media from the perspective of a mere consumer of information, readers must learn to actively and dynamically engage with it while trying to make sense of it.

information evaluation ought to be completed in a single step
lateral reading requires ongoing and repeated evaluation of information

body:
[1]
Numerous surveys consistently highlight the growing trend of teenagers spending extensive hours on social media. This increased usage comes with potential risks, including addiction and exposure to misinformation and inappropriate content. Many adolescents struggle with managing their time and interactions on social media. To address these concerns, certain authorities are implementing legal restrictions on minors’ access to social media. For example, in some countries, like China, limits for social media have been put on children and teens. Also, in 2023, the state of Utah enacted two bills: one requiring parental consent for minors to create or maintain social media accounts and the other granting parents full access to their children’s online activities.
[2]
Despite these concerns, it is crucial to maintain a balanced perspective that acknowledges the significant advantages that social media can offer. Social media provides an efficient platform for teenagers to express themselves, discover new friendships, and connect with like-minded individuals. Through sharing their thoughts, experiences, and talents, they can find a sense of empowerment and self-identity in the digital world. Research shows the benefits of social media in fostering peer connections and offering essential emotional support, particularly for teens who may lack such support within their local communities. Additionally, social media serves as a valuable tool for staying informed about current events and acquiring knowledge on various subjects, making it an invaluable resource for research and problem-solving.
[3]
As we weigh these contrasting effects of social media, the question of whether regulating teenagers’ social media usage should remain a private or public matter is left open. This debate shows the fundamental tension between personal freedoms and societal interests, and it is one that continues to evolve with the ever-changing digital landscape. It is certainly worth reflecting on. Which side of this debate do you find yourself on, and what drives your perspective?
윗글의 내용과 (A)~(E)가 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 쓸 때, 순서대로 연결된 것은?
(A) Surveys indicate that teenagers are increasingly spending long periods on social media, which may expose them to various risks. (T/F)
(B) Some governments have introduced restrictions on minors’ social media use to address problems related to their online activities. (T/F)
(C) Social media can help teenagers develop a sense of identity and receive emotional support, especially when such support is limited in their communities. (T/F)
(D) Social media has little educational value beyond personal expression and social interaction. (T/F)
(E) The debate over teenagers’ social media use has begun to prioritize the benefits of social media over its potential risks. (T/F)

To address these concerns, certain authorities are implementing legal restrictions on minors’ access to social media. For example, in some countries, like China, limits for social media have been put on children and teens. Also, in 2023, the state of Utah enacted two bills: one requiring parental consent for minors to create or maintain social media accounts and the other granting parents full access to their children’s online activities.
[2]
Despite these concerns, it is crucial to maintain a balanced perspective that acknowledges the significant advantages that social media can offer. Social media provides an efficient platform for teenagers to express themselves, discover new friendships, and connect with like-minded individuals. Through sharing their thoughts, experiences, and talents, they can find a sense of empowerment and self-identity in the digital world. Research shows the benefits of social media in fostering peer connections and offering essential emotional support, particularly for teens who may lack such support within their local communities. Additionally, social media serves as a valuable tool for staying informed about current events and acquiring knowledge on various subjects, making it an invaluable resource for research and problem-solving.
[3]
As we weigh these contrasting effects of social media, the question of whether regulating teenagers’ social media usage should remain a private or public matter is left open. This debate shows the fundamental tension between personal freedoms and societal interests, and it is one that continues to evolve with the ever-changing digital landscape. It is certainly worth reflecting on. Which side of this debate do you find yourself on, and what drives your perspective?

the correlation between online participation and youth identity development
fostering teenagers’ face-to-face communication skills through group activities
improving teenagers’ academic focus through modern digital learning tools
the benefits of social media for teenagers’ personal, social, and intellectual development

In a place called Cottingley, England, in 1917, two young girls took some pictures of themselves near a stream at the bottom of a garden. The pictures showed the girls playing with fairies. When the famous author of Sherlock Holmes, Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, found out about them, he wrote an article claiming that the pictures were proof of supernatural phenomena. In today’s words, one could say that the pictures went “viral,” and Doyle’s (A)[endorsement / skepticism] gave the pictures “credibility.” For several years, the girls maintained that the pictures were genuine. Only after almost seventy years did the girls finally admit that the whole thing was (B)[authentic / fabricated]. While this story is an interesting anecdote of fake news involving a famous author, it may be a cautionary tale demonstrating the importance of media literacy in the digital age.
Single-Source Reading
In the past, knowledge was passed down directly by the spoken word. The credibility of the speaker, not what was said, was the measure of trustworthiness. When the printing press introduced books as a means of knowledge transfer and written materials became more (C)[prevalent / limited], readers had to develop new critical evaluation skills. However, they were often limited to a single source to evaluate the writer’s credibility, arguments, and logic. This type of analysis can be described as “vertical reading.”
다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: skepticism / fabricated / limited
endorsement / fabricated / limited
skepticism / authentic / prevalent
endorsement / authentic / limited
endorsement / fabricated / prevalent
solution:
(A) 앞에서 Doyle이 요정들과 함께 찍은 사진들이 초자연적 현상의 증거라고 주장하는 기사를 썼다고 했으므로, 그의 지지가 소녀들의 사진들에 신뢰성을 부여했다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 endorsement(지지)가 적절하다.
(B) 이 사진과 관련된 사건을 유명한 작가가 관련된 가짜 뉴스의 한 일화로 소개하고 있으므로 소녀들이 그 사진이 진짜라고 주장하다가 거의 70년이 지나서야 꾸며낸 것이었다고 인정했다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 fabricated(꾸며낸)가 적절하다.
(C) 인쇄기의 등장으로 책이 지식 전달 수단이 되었다고 설명하고 있으므로 문서 자료들이 더 널리 보급되었다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 prevalent(널리 퍼진)가 적절하다.

body:
Readers employing digital lateral reading can take advantage of the volume of information on the Internet to check the credibility of an author’s claims. They can utilize Internet browser tools that help review many sites simultaneously. Many people and companies currently use this reading strategy because it allows them to more easily cross-check data, distinguish opinions from facts, and evaluate claims efficiently.
As a way to maintain credibility, some companies hire “fact-checkers” to evaluate their writers’ claims before publishing anything. These fact-checkers use lateral reading as a quick means to survey what has already been written. For example, imagine a news agency that wants to publish a story on its website about a merger between two corporations. Fact-checkers will cross-check information from a variety of sources to ensure that the facts are accurate. In fact, in recent research surveys, having utilized this strategy, participants were found to have a broader understanding of any kind of information than participants who had used less optimal strategies like vertical reading.

choices: What does digital lateral reading enable readers to do to check the credibility of an author’s claims?
Why do many people and companies adopt lateral reading as their reading strategy?
What information helps readers decide which online sources are worth examining?
What specific role do "fact-checkers" play in media companies before publishing content?
What did recent research reveal about lateral reading compared to vertical reading?

body:
Multiple-Source Reading
Vertical reading is still useful, but new strategies must be adopted to navigate the vast online world. One of these strategies is called “lateral reading,” which involves verifying information while (A)[reading / read] by checking as many sources as you can. This is useful because only one source is not enough. Checking information from multiple sources with various types of content, such as text, images, and videos, is helpful to verify something (B)[what / that] you have read and gain insight.
For example, suppose a student reads an article on a popular online news site about the health of a population of people. Having come across some statistics about the number of people who are hospitalized due to poor diet, she can employ the lateral reading strategy by simply opening up another tab in her browser and accessing different sources to verify the numbers. In fact, she can open up as many new tabs as she wants to verify any type of information (C)[presenting / being presented], such as statistics in charts and tables, or general assertions. She can look up information from other popular news sites or go directly to a scientific journal article to read from the primary source of information.

reading / what / being presented
reading / that / presenting
solution:

(B) 동사 read의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(you have read)을 이끌어 선행사 something을 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로 목적격 관계대명사 that이 적절하다.
*(B)는 본문에서 생략되었음

When the printing press introduced books as a means of knowledge transfer and ⓑwritten materials became more prevalent, readers had to develop new critical evaluation skills. However, they were often limited to a single source to evaluate the writer’s credibility, arguments, and logic. This type of analysis can be described as “vertical reading.”
Vertical reading involves relying on the text ⓒto determine the reliability or validity of information. In school, students learn to examine an author’s credibility, their logic, and their references based on only their text. ⓓHaving read a book, for example, a reader can review if the arguments presented in the text ⓔis supported by enough evidence, look at who the author or the publisher is, or check the references cited in the text. However, technology has changed the landscape in which people write and publish, so this ⓕmaking it necessary to change reading strategies.

solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓔ is → are (주어가 과거분사구 presented in the text의 수식을 받는 복수명사구 the arguments이므로 is를 be동사 복수형인 are로 고친다.)
ⓕ making → makes (접속사 so, 주어 this에 이어지는 동사 자리이며, 앞 절의 내용인 ‘기술이 사람들이 글을 쓰고 출판하는 환경을 변화시킨 것’이 읽기 전략을 바꾸게 하는 주체이고 변화로 인한 현재 시점의 필요성을 언급하고 있으므로 현재시제로 써야 한다. 따라서 making을 현재시제 makes로 고친다.)
본문변형 , making it ~ → , so this makes it ~
오답
ⓐ 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(was said)을 이끌어 주어와 동사 사이에 이중 콤마로 삽입되어 주어인 The credibility of the speaker와 대조 관계를 이루어 부연 설명하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사 what은 적절하다.
ⓑ 이어지는 명사 materials를 수식하는 분사 자리이며 수식을 받는 materials가 ‘쓰인‘ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 written은 적절하다.
ⓒ 완전한 절(Vertical ~ text)에 접속사 없이 이어지므로 준동사 자리이며, 흐름상 ’신뢰성이나 타당성을 판단하기 위해‘라는 뜻으로 목적을 나타내야 하므로 부사적 용법의 to부정사 to determine은 적절하다.
ⓓ 완전한 절 앞에 콤마로만 연결되어 있으므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, ’책을 읽은 것‘이 주절의 내용(독자가 검토하고, 살펴보고, 확인하는 것)보다 먼저 일어난 일이므로 완료형 분사구문을 이루는 완료형 분사의 형태로 써야 한다. 또한 의미상 주어인 a reader가 책을 ’읽는‘ 주체이므로 완료형 분사의 능동태(having p.p.)인 Having read는 적절하다.

Readers employing digital lateral reading can take advantage of the ⓐvolume of information on the Internet to check the credibility of an author’s claims. They can utilize Internet browser tools that help review many sites ⓑsimultaneously. Many people and companies currently use this reading strategy because it allows them to more easily ⓒcross-check data, distinguish opinions from facts, and evaluate claims efficiently.
As a way to maintain credibility, some companies hire “fact-checkers” to evaluate their writers’ claims before publishing anything. (A)이 사실 확인자들은 이미 작성된 것을 조사할 신속한 수단으로 가로 읽기를 활용한다. For example, imagine a news agency that wants to publish a story on its website about a merger between two corporations. Fact-checkers will cross-check information from a variety of sources to ensure that the facts are accurate. In fact, in recent research surveys, having utilized this strategy, participants were found to have a ⓓnarrower understanding of any kind of information than participants who had used less optimal strategies like ⓔvertical reading.

body:
Vertical reading is not a perfect strategy and neither ⓐdoes lateral reading, but lateral reading takes greater advantage of modern technology than vertical reading. To fully appreciate this strategy, a reader in the digital world makes evaluating all forms of information a habit. ⓑNo matter how neutral an author or publication claims to be, the burden of evaluation falls upon the reader to survey as much information as possible to determine the credibility of the data or the claims. We need to understand ⓒthat the world, and therefore information itself, is constantly evolving: information does not remain still, so ⓓneither should the reader. For this reason, lateral reading is a continuous, repetitive process. Instead of approaching media from the perspective of a mere consumer of information, readers must learn to actively and dynamically engage with it while ⓔtrying to make sense of it.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓐ does → is (부정문의 뒤에 접속사 and로 neither로 시작하는 절이 쓰여 ‘~도 … 아니다’라는 의미를 나타내고 있다. 부정의 의미를 포함하는 neither로 시작하는 절에서는 주어와 동사의 순서가 바뀌는 도치가 발생하므로 ‘neither+동사+주어’의 어순으로 쓴 것은 알맞으나 and 앞 절에서 be동사 is가 쓰였으며 주어가 단수명사구인 lateral reading이므로 does를 be동사 단수형인 is로 고친다.)
오답
ⓑ 주절(the burden ~ the claims) 앞에서 콤마(,)로 연결되어 「no matter how+형용사+주어+동사」 구조의 양보의 부사절을 이루는 ‘아무리 ~할지라도’라는 뜻의 no matter how는 적절하다.
ⓒ understand의 목적어 자리에서 완전한 절(the world ~ evolving)을 이끌어 명사절을 이루고 있으므로 접속사 that은 적절하다.
ⓓ 정보가 정체되어 있지 않다는 부정문 ‘information does not remain still’에 이어지고 있으며 ‘조동사+주어’의 어순으로 도치된 should the reader가 이어지고 있으므로 부정문의 뒤에서 ‘…도 또한 ~하지 않는다’라는 뜻을 이루는 neither는 적절하다.
ⓔ 접속사 while 뒤에 주어와 동사가 없으므로 접속사 while을 생략하지 않은 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 의미상 주어인 readers가 ‘애쓰는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미를 갖는 현재분사 trying은 적절하다.

(B)

다음 글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘더불어, 소셜 미디어는 시사에 대한 정보를 얻고 다양한 주제의 지식을 습득하는 데 유용한 도구로 쓰이며, 이는 연구 및 문제 해결을 위한 귀중한 자원이 된다.’라는 뜻으로, 소셜 미디어의 장점을 추가로 언급하고 있다. 연결어 Additionally(더불어)가 쓰였으므로 이 문장 앞에는 소셜 미디어의 장점을 설명하는 내용이 와야 한다. (B) 앞에서는 소셜 미디어가 또래와의 연결을 촉진하고 정서적 지지를 제공하는 데 도움이 된다는 연구 결과를 제시하고 있으며, (B) 이하에는 소셜 미디어의 상반된 영향으로 인해 소셜 미디어의 사용을 규제하는 것이 개인의 문제인지 공공의 문제인지에 대한 질문이 열려 있다는 내용이 이어지고 있으므로 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은 (B)이다.

In a place called Cottingley, England, in 1917, two young girls took some pictures of themselves near a stream at the bottom of a garden. The pictures showed the girls playing with fairies. When the famous author of Sherlock Holmes, Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, found out about them, he wrote an article claiming that the pictures were proof of supernatural phenomena. In today’s words, one could say that the pictures went “viral,” and Doyle’s endorsement gave the pictures “credibility.” For several years, the girls maintained that the pictures were genuine. Only after almost seventy years did the girls finally admit that the whole thing was made up. While this story is an interesting anecdote of fake news involving a famous author, it may be a cautionary tale ______ in the digital age.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: representing the influence of technology on the spread of false information
illustrating the benefits of sharing information with a wider audience
suggesting the importance of trusting information endorsed by experts
explaining how digital tools can help distinguish fact from fiction
emphasizing the necessity of critically evaluating information
solution:
유명 작가인 Arthur Conan Doyle이 사진을 초자연적 현상의 증거라고 주장하면서 사진에 신뢰성을 부여했지만, 오랜 시간이 지난 후 소녀들이 사진이 조작된 것이었음을 인정했으므로, 유명 인사의 지지가 있더라도 정보를 무조건 신뢰해서는 안 된다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ⑤ ‘정보를 비판적으로 평가할 필요성을 강조하는’이 적절하다.
본문변형 demonstrating the importance of media literacy → emphasizing the necessity of critically evaluating information

(A) When the famous author of Sherlock Holmes, Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, found out about them, he wrote an article claiming that the pictures were proof of supernatural phenomena. (B) For several years, the girls maintained that the pictures were genuine. (C) Only after almost seventy years did the girls finally admit that the whole thing was made up. (D) While this story is an interesting anecdote of fake news involving a famous author, it may be a cautionary tale demonstrating the importance of media literacy in the digital age. (E)

In today’s words, one could say that the pictures went “viral,” and Doyle’s endorsement gave the pictures “credibility.”

윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘오늘날 표현으로는, 그 사진들은 ‘입소문을 타고 퍼졌다’고 할 상황이었고, 도일의 지지는 이 사진들에 ‘신뢰성’을 부여해 주었다.’라는 뜻으로 이 문장 앞에는 the pictures(그 사진들)라고 지칭할 수 있는 특정 사진들이 언급되어야 하고, 도일이 그 사진들을 지지했다는 내용이 와야 한다. (A) 앞에서 소녀들과 요정들이 함께 있는 사진이 언급되었고, (B) 앞에서는 도일이 해당 사진을 초자연적 현상의 증거라고 주장하는 기사를 썼다고 설명하고 있다. 이는 사진이 널리 퍼지고 신뢰성을 얻는 계기가 되었음을 의미하므로 이 문장 뒤에 주어진 문장이 오면 자연스럽게 연결된다. 따라서 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은 (B)이다.

body:
In the past, knowledge was passed down directly by the spoken word. The credibility of the speaker, not what was said, was the measure of trustworthiness. When the printing press introduced books as a means of knowledge transfer and written materials became more prevalent, readers had to develop new critical evaluation skills.
(A) Vertical reading involves relying on the text to determine the reliability or validity of information. In school, students learn to examine an author’s credibility, their logic, and their references based on only their text.
(B) However, they were often limited to a single source to evaluate the writer’s credibility, arguments, and logic. This type of analysis can be described as “vertical reading.”
(C) Having read a book, for example, a reader can review if the arguments presented in the text are supported by enough evidence, look at who the author or the publisher is, or check the references cited in the text.
However, technology has changed the landscape in which people write and publish, making it necessary to change reading strategies.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 인쇄술의 발달로 책이 지식 전달의 수단이 되면서 독자들이 새로운 비판적 평가 능력을 개발해야 했다는 주어진 글 뒤에 앞 문장에서 언급된 readers를 they로 받고, 역접의 연결어 However(하지만)를 통해 그들이 저자의 신뢰성, 주장, 논리를 평가할 때 하나의 출처에 의존하는 경우가 많았다는 한계를 지적하는 (B), (B)의 마지막에서 처음 언급된 vertical reading(세로 읽기)의 개념을 설명하고, 학교에서 학생들이 글만을 바탕으로 저자의 신뢰성, 논리, 참고 자료를 검토한다고 언급하는 (A), For example(예를 들어)을 통해 책을 읽은 독자가 주장의 근거, 저자나 출판사, 참고 자료를 확인하는 방법을 구체적인 예시로 제시하는 (C)로 이어지는 흐름이 자연스럽다.

Readers ⓐemploying digital lateral reading can take advantage of the volume of information on the Internet ⓑto check the credibility of an author’s claims. They can utilize Internet browser tools that help (A)______. Many people and companies currently use this reading strategy because it allows them to more easily cross-check data, ⓒdistinguish opinions from facts, and evaluate claims efficiently.
As a way to maintain credibility, some companies hire “fact-checkers” to evaluate their writers’ claims before publishing anything. These fact-checkers use lateral reading as a quick means to survey ⓓthat has already been written. For example, imagine a news agency that wants to publish a story on its website about a merger between two corporations. Fact-checkers will cross-check information from a variety of sources to ensure ⓔwhat the facts are accurate. In fact, in recent research surveys, having utilized this strategy, participants were found to have a broader understanding of any kind of information than participants who ⓕhad used less optimal strategies like vertical reading.

solution:

ⓔ what → that (완전한 절(the facts are accurate)을 이끌어 ensure의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 what을 명사절 접속사 that으로 고친다.)

ⓒ 동사 allow는 ’allow+목적어+목적격보어’의 5형식 구문으로 쓸 때, 목적격보어로 to부정사를 취하므로 단수동사 allows와 목적어 them에 이어지는 목적격보어 자리에서 분리부정사(to+부사+동사원형)를 이루는 동사원형 cross-check와 콤마로 연결되어 있으며 접속사 and로 동사원형 evaluate이 이어져 ‘A, B, and C’의 형태로 병렬 구조를 이루는 동사원형 distinguish는 적절하다.
ⓕ 참가자들이 덜 효과적인 전략을 사용한 것이 최근 연구 조사에 의해 밝혀진 것(were found)보다 먼저 발생한 일이므로 과거완료 시제인 had used는 적절하다.

Numerous surveys consistently highlight the growing trend of teenagers spending extensive hours on social media. This increased usage comes with potential risks, including addiction and exposure to misinformation and inappropriate content. Many adolescents struggle with managing their time and interactions on social media. To address these concerns, certain authorities are implementing legal restrictions on minors’ access to social media. (A)______, in some countries, like China, limits for social media ⓐhave been put on children and teens. Also, in 2023, the state of Utah enacted two bills: one requiring parental consent for minors to create or ⓑmaintaining social media accounts and the other granting parents full access to their children’s online activities.
Despite these concerns, it is crucial to maintain a balanced perspective ⓒthat acknowledges the significant advantages that social media can offer. Social media provides an efficient platform for teenagers to express themselves, discover new friendships, and connect with like-minded individuals. Through sharing their thoughts, experiences, and talents, they can find a sense of empowerment and self-identity in the digital world. Research shows the benefits of social media in fostering peer connections and ⓓoffers essential emotional support, particularly for teens who may lack such support within their local communities. (B)______, social media serves as a valuable tool for staying informed about current events and acquiring knowledge on various subjects, making it an invaluable resource for research and problem-solving.
As we weigh these contrasting effects of social media, the question of whether ⓔregulating teenagers’ social media usage should remain a private or public matter is left open. This debate shows the fundamental tension between personal freedoms and societal interests, and it is one that continues to evolve with the ever-changing digital landscape. It is certainly worth reflecting on. Which side of this debate do you find yourself on, and what drives your perspective?

In today’s words, one could say ⓒthat the pictures went “viral,” and Doyle’s endorsement gave the pictures “credibility.” For several years, the girls maintained that the pictures were genuine. Only after almost seventy years did the girls finally ⓓadmitted that the whole thing was made up. While this story is an interesting anecdote of fake news involving a famous author, it may be a cautionary tale ⓔdemonstrating the importance of media literacy in the digital age.

In a place ⓐcalled Cottingley, England, in 1917, two young girls took some pictures of themselves near a stream at the bottom of a garden. The pictures showed the girls playing with fairies. When the famous author of Sherlock Holmes, Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, found out about them, he wrote an article ⓑclaiming that the pictures were proof of supernatural phenomena. In today’s words, one could say ⓒthat the pictures went “viral,” and Doyle’s endorsement gave the pictures “credibility.” For several years, the girls maintained that the pictures were genuine. Only after almost seventy years did the girls finally ⓓadmitted that the whole thing was made up. While this story is an interesting anecdote of fake news involving a famous author, it may be a cautionary tale ⓔdemonstrating the importance of media literacy in the digital age.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: what draws the public to stories of the supernatural
the influence of a famous writer's endorsement on public belief
why verifying the authenticity of historical photographs is difficult
the importance of critically evaluating information before accepting it as true
the development of media literacy through studying historical photographs

Single-Source Reading

In the past, knowledge was passed down directly by the spoken word. The credibility of the speaker, not what was said, ⓐwas the measure of trustworthiness. When the printing press introduced books as a means of knowledge transfer and written materials became more prevalent, readers had to develop new critical evaluation skills. However, they were often limited to a single source to evaluate the writer’s credibility, arguments, and logic. This type of analysis can ⓑbe described as “vertical reading.”
Vertical reading involves relying on the text to determine the reliability or validity of information. In school, students learn to examine an author’s credibility, their logic, and their references based on only their text. ⓒHaving read a book, for example, a reader can review if the arguments presented in the text are supported by enough evidence, look at who the author or the publisher is, or ⓓcheck the references cited in the text. However, technology has changed the landscape ⓔwhich people write and publish, making it necessary to change reading strategies.

Since technology in 1917 was nowhere near as advanced as it is today, it’s understandable that a few pictures could convince a famous author as well as the general public of the existence of fairies. (A) Does advanced technology prevent people from being fooled now? (B) Many people today fall victim to hoaxes or accept false claims because they don’t know how to verify information. (C) This begs the question: How is it possible to verify such vast amounts of information? (D) On the Internet, finding information is relatively easy, but verifying or validating it is not. (E) In the past, there were publishing standards that authors had to meet. Today, the Internet removes the barriers to publishing for millions of people; however, it also makes it harder for readers to find reliable and valid information. In this environment, media literacy is more important than ever.

In fact, it may make it even easier to get tricked.

윗글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘사실, 그것은 오히려 더 속기 쉽게 만들 수도 있다.’라는 뜻으로 주어진 문장의 주어인 it이 (B) 앞의 advanced technology(첨단 기술)을 가리키고 있으므로 첨단 기술이 오늘날 사람들이 속는 것을 막아 주는지 질문하는 내용 뒤이자 사람들이 오늘날 많은 사람들이 정보를 검증하는 방법을 몰라 속임수의 피해자가 되거나 거짓 주장을 받아들인다는 내용 앞인 (B)에 들어가야 한다.

body:
Multiple-Source Reading

Vertical reading is still useful, but new strategies must be adopted to navigate the vast online world. One of these strategies is called “lateral reading,” (A)[which / that] involves verifying information while reading by checking as many sources as you can. This is useful because only one source is not enough. (B)[Checking / Check] information from multiple sources with various types of content, such as text, images, and videos, is helpful to verify something you have read and (C)[gains / gain] insight.
For example, suppose a student reads an article on a popular online news site about the health of a population of people. Having come across some statistics about the number of people who are hospitalized due to poor diet, she can employ the lateral reading strategy by simply opening up another tab in her browser and accessing different sources to verify the numbers. In fact, she can open up as many new tabs as she wants to verify any type of information being presented, such as statistics in charts and tables, or general assertions. She can look up information from other popular news sites or go directly to a scientific journal article to read from the primary source of information.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: which Checking gains
that Checking gains
that Check gains
which Check gain
which Checking gain

(B) 뒤에 동사 is가 있으므로 이어지는 명사구를 목적어로 취하여 주어부를 이루는 준동사 자리이다. 따라서 동명사 Checking이 적절하다.
(C) 형용사 helpful을 수식하는 부사적 용법의 to부정사 to verify와 등위접속사 and로 병렬 연결되어야 하므로 to를 생략한 동사원형 gain이 적절하다. 이처럼 to부정사의 병렬구조에서 두 번째 to는 흔히 생략된다.

Readers ⓐemploying digital lateral reading can take advantage of the volume of information on the Internet to check the ⓑcredibility of an author’s claims. They can utilize Internet browser tools that help review many sites simultaneously. Many people and companies currently use this reading strategy because it allows them to more easily ⓒcross-check data, distinguish opinions from facts, and evaluate ⓓclaims efficiently.
As a way to maintain credibility, some companies hire “fact-checkers” to evaluate their writers’ claims before publishing anything. These fact-checkers use ⓔlateral reading as a quick means to survey what has already been written. For example, imagine a news agency that wants to publish a story on its website about a merger between two corporations. Fact-checkers will cross-check information from a variety of sources to ensure that the facts are accurate. In fact, in recent research surveys, (A)이 전략을 활용한 참가자들이 세로 읽기와 같이 덜 효과적인 전략들을 사용한 참가자들보다 어떤 정보든 더 폭넓은 이해를 하는 것으로 밝혀졌다.

Numerous surveys consistently highlight the growing trend of teenagers spending extensive hours on social media. This increased usage comes with potential risks, including addiction and exposure to misinformation and inappropriate content. Many adolescents struggle with managing their time and interactions on social media. To address these concerns, certain authorities are implementing legal restrictions on minors’ access to social media. For example, in some countries, like China, limits for social media have been put on children and teens. Also, in 2023, the state of Utah enacted two bills: one requiring parental consent for minors to create or (A)[maintain / maintaining] social media accounts and the other granting parents full access to their children’s online activities.
Despite these concerns, it is crucial (B)[maintain / to maintain] a balanced perspective that acknowledges the significant advantages that social media can offer. Social media provides an efficient platform for teenagers to express themselves, discover new friendships, and connect with like-minded individuals. Through sharing their thoughts, experiences, and talents, they can find a sense of empowerment and self-identity in the digital world. Research shows the benefits of social media in fostering peer connections and offering essential emotional support, particularly for teens who may lack such support within their local communities. Additionally, social media serves as a valuable tool for staying informed about current events and acquiring knowledge on various subjects, (C)[making / make] it an invaluable resource for research and problem-solving.
As we weigh these contrasting effects of social media, the question of whether regulating teenagers’ social media usage should remain a private or public matter is left open. This debate shows the fundamental tension between personal freedoms and societal interests, and it is one that continues to evolve with the ever-changing digital landscape. It is certainly worth reflecting on. Which side of this debate do you find yourself on, and what drives your perspective?

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: maintaining maintain making
maintain to maintain make
maintaining to maintain making
maintain maintain make
maintain to maintain making
solution:
(A) 앞의 명사구 parental consent를 수식하는 형용사적 용법의 to부정사 to create와 등위접속사 or로 병렬 연결되어야 하므로 to를 생략한 동사원형 maintain이 적절하다.
(B) 가주어 it에 상응하는 진주어 자리이므로 to부정사 to maintain이 적절하다.
(C) 완전한 절(social ~ subjects)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 이어지므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 주절의 내용인 소셜 미디어가 시사에 대한 정보를 얻고 다양한 주제의 정보를 습득하는 데 유용한 도구로 쓰이는 것이 목적어인 it이 가리키는 social media를 귀중한 자원으로 ‘만드는’ 주체이므로 능동의 의미인 현재분사 making이 적절하다.

body:
Numerous surveys consistently highlight the growing trend of teenagers spending extensive hours on social media. This increased usage comes with potential risks, including addiction and exposure to misinformation and inappropriate content. Many adolescents struggle with managing their time and interactions on social media. To address these concerns, certain authorities are implementing legal restrictions on minors’ access to social media. For example, in some countries, like China, limits for social media have been put on children and teens. Also, in 2023, the state of Utah enacted two bills: one requiring parental consent for minors to create or (A)[maintain / maintaining] social media accounts and the other granting parents full access to their children’s online activities.
Despite these concerns, it is crucial (B)[maintain / to maintain] a balanced perspective that acknowledges the significant advantages that social media can offer. Social media provides an efficient platform for teenagers to express themselves, discover new friendships, and connect with like-minded individuals. Through sharing their thoughts, experiences, and talents, they can find a sense of empowerment and self-identity in the digital world. Research shows the benefits of social media in fostering peer connections and offering essential emotional support, particularly for teens who may lack such support within their local communities. Additionally, social media serves as a valuable tool for staying informed about current events and acquiring knowledge on various subjects, (C)[making / make] it an invaluable resource for research and problem-solving.
As we weigh these contrasting effects of social media, the question of whether regulating teenagers’ social media usage should remain a private or public matter is left open. This debate shows the fundamental tension between personal freedoms and societal interests, and it is one that continues to evolve with the ever-changing digital landscape. It is certainly worth reflecting on. Which side of this debate do you find yourself on, and what drives your perspective?

윗글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
Although concerns about the risks of teenagers' social media use have led to ______ restrictions, social media also offers ______ such as self-expression, ______ support, and access to information, which raises the question of whether its regulation should be a ______ or ______ matter.
solution: [요약문] 십 대의 소셜 미디어 사용에 따른 위험성에 대한 우려가 법적 규제로 이어졌지만, 소셜 미디어는 자기표현, 정서적 지원, 정보 접근과 같은 이점들도 제공하며, 이는 소셜 미디어 사용에 대한 규제가 개인의 문제인지 공적인 문제인지에 관한 의문을 제기한다.

body:
ⓐ세로 읽기는 완벽한 전략이 아니며, 가로 읽기도 마찬가지지만, 가로 읽기는 세로 읽기보다 현대 기술을 보다 더 효과적으로 활용한다. To fully appreciate this strategy, a reader in the digital world makes evaluating all forms of information a habit. (A) No matter how neutral an author or publication claims to be, the burden of evaluation falls upon the reader to survey as much information as possible to determine the credibility of the data or the claims. (B) We need to understand that the world, and therefore information itself, is constantly evolving: information does not remain still, so neither should the reader. (C) For this reason, lateral reading is a continuous, repetitive process. (D) Furthermore, the rapid advancement of digital technology has enabled consumers to access a wider range of entertainment media than ever before. (E) Instead of approaching media from the perspective of a mere consumer of information, readers must learn to actively and dynamically engage with it while trying to make sense of it.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E) 중, 흐름상 관계없는 문장은?
solution: 디지털 시대에 정보의 신뢰성을 판단하기 위한 가로 읽기와 독자의 능동적인 정보 평가 자세를 설명하는 글이다. (A)는 정보의 신뢰성을 판단할 책임이 독자에게 있음을 강조하고, (B)는 정보가 끊임없이 변화한다는 점을 언급하며, (C)는 이에 대응하기 위해 가로 읽기가 지속적이고 반복적인 과정이어야 함을 설명하고, (E)는 독자가 정보를 수동적으로 소비하는 데 그치지 않고 능동적으로 탐색하고 이해해야 함을 강조한다. 그러나 (D) ‘게다가, 디지털 기술의 급격한 발전은 소비자들이 그 어느 때보다 더 광범위한 엔터테인먼트 미디어에 접근할 수 있게 해주었다.’는 비판적 정보 검증 및 가로 읽기와는 무관하므로 글의 흐름과 관계없다.

body:
In the past, knowledge was passed down directly by the spoken word. The credibility of the speaker, not what was said, was the measure of trustworthiness. When the printing press introduced books as a means of knowledge transfer and written materials became more prevalent, readers had to develop new critical evaluation skills. However, they were often limited to a single source to evaluate the writer’s credibility, arguments, and logic. This type of analysis can be described as “vertical reading.”
Vertical reading ______ to determine the reliability or validity of information. In school, students learn to examine an author’s credibility, their logic, and their references based on only their text. Having read a book, for example, a reader can review if the arguments presented in the text are supported by enough evidence, look at who the author or the publisher is, or check the references cited in the text. However, technology has changed the landscape in which people write and publish, making it necessary to change reading strategies.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: requires checking multiple online sources
depends on judging a speaker’s reputation
encourages changes in reading strategies
focuses on the author’s writing style
involves relying on the text
solution:
앞에서 세로 읽기는 저자의 신뢰성, 주장, 논리를 평가하기 위해 하나의 출처만을 활용하는 분석 방법이라고 설명하고, 뒤에서도 독자가 원문에 제시된 근거와 참고 자료 등을 검토한다고 했으므로 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ⑤ ‘원문에 의존하는 것을 포함한다’가 적절하다.

③ 읽기 전략의 변화를 장려한다
④ 저자의 글쓰기 방식에 초점을 맞춘다

body:
In a place called Cottingley, England, in 1917, two young girls took some pictures of themselves near a stream at the bottom of a garden. The pictures showed the girls playing with fairies. When the famous author of Sherlock Holmes, Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, found out about them, he wrote an article claiming that the pictures were proof of (A)[natural / supernatural] phenomena. In today’s words, one could say that the pictures went “viral,” and Doyle’s endorsement gave the pictures “credibility.” For several years, the girls maintained that the pictures were (B)[fake / genuine]. Only after almost seventy years did the girls finally admit that the whole thing was made up. While this story is an interesting anecdote of fake news involving a famous author, it may be a cautionary tale (C)[demonstrating / undermining] the importance of media literacy in the digital age.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: supernatural genuine undermining
natural fake demonstrating
supernatural fake undermining
supernatural genuine demonstrating
natural genuine demonstrating
solution:
(A) 사진은 소녀들이 요정들과 함께 노는 모습을 담고 있었다고 했으므로 초자연적인 현상이라는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 supernatural(초자연적인)이 적절하다.
natural 자연의
(B) 뒤에서 거의 70년이 지난 뒤 소녀들이 모든 것이 다 꾸며낸 일이었다고 인정했다고 했으므로 이 사진들이 진짜라고 주장했다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 genuine(진짜의)이 적절하다.
fake 가짜의
(C) 두 소녀가 사진을 조작하고 유명 작가의 주장이 사진에 신뢰성을 부여하여 사람들이 이를 믿게 되었다고 했으므로, 이것이 디지털 시대에 미디어 리터러시가 중요하다는 점을 보여 준다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 demonstrating(보여주는)이 적절하다.
undermine ~을 약화시키다

body:
Since technology in 1917 was nowhere near as advanced as it is today, it’s understandable that a few pictures could convince a famous author as well as the general public of the existence of fairies. Does advanced technology prevent people from being fooled now? In fact, it may make it even easier to (A)______. Many people today fall victim to hoaxes or accept false claims because they don’t know how to verify information.
This begs the question: How is it possible to verify such vast amounts of information? On the Internet, finding information is relatively easy, but (B)______. In the past, there were publishing standards that authors had to meet. Today, the Internet removes the barriers to publishing for millions of people; however, it also makes it harder for readers to find reliable and valid information. In this environment, media literacy is more important than ever.

다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
choices:
(A) verify information
(B) verifying or validating it is not

(A) get tricked
(B) most users can access it without difficulty

(A) verify information
(B) sharing it takes little effort

(A) get tricked
(B) verifying or validating it is not

(A) adopt advanced technology
(B) most users can access it without difficulty
solution:
(A) 앞에서 첨단 기술이 오늘날 사람들이 속지 않도록 막아 줄 수 있는지 질문하고, 뒤에서 많은 사람이 정보를 검증하는 방법을 몰라 속임수에 넘어가거나 거짓 주장을 받아들인다고 설명하므로, 오히려 더 쉽게 속게 될 수 있다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 get tricked(속아 넘어가다)가 적절하다.
(B) 인터넷에서 정보를 찾는 것이 비교적 쉽다는 내용과 역접의 연결사인 but으로 연결되어 있으며, 과거와 달리 출판 장벽은 사라졌지만 독자들이 신뢰할 수 있고 타당한 정보를 찾는 일이 더 어려워 졌다는 내용이 이어지고 있으므로 인터넷에서 발견할 수 있는 정보를 검증하는 것은 어렵다는 흐름이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 verifying or validating it is not(그것을 검증하거나 그 타당성을 확인하는 것은 그렇지 않다)이 적절하다.
오답
① (A) 정보를 검증하다
(B) 그것을 검증하거나 그 타당성을 확인하는 것은 그렇지 않다
② (A) 속아 넘어가다
(B) 대부분의 이용자들은 어려움 없이 그것에 접근할 수 있다
③ (A) 정보를 검증하다
(B) 그것을 공유하는 데는 노력이 거의 들지 않는다
⑤ (A) 첨단 기술을 채택하다
(B) 대부분의 이용자들은 어려움 없이 그것에 접근할 수 있다

body:
W: Good afternoon, students! Do you want to make your lunch break more valuable? Then join our on-campus lunchtime walking group and experience the magnificent benefits of taking a casual walk during your break. Do you know the Latin phrase, “Solvitur Ambulando”? It’s all about resolving problems by merely walking. Even research backs it up! Walking after eating fires up your metabolism, helps with the breakdown of food, and increases your energy. But that’s not all! When you walk outside, your stress goes down, your mood gets a sunny boost, and your brain gets sharper. It’s like a stress-relieving and mood-boosting therapy session in nature’s playground. I hope you’ll enjoy these benefits with our walking group! So put on your sneakers and make lunchtime the highlight of your day!

다음 담화의 목적으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: to advise students to exercise during their lunch break
to explain how to relieve stress through walking outside
to inform students about the benefits of walking after lunch
to encourage students to join the lunchtime walking group
to announce a new schedule for the campus walking group
solution:
담화의 초반부에 학교 점심시간 산책 모임에 참여해보라고 권유하고, 쉬는 시간에 가볍게 산책하는 것의 이점을 설명한 뒤 마지막에 다시 한 번 산책 모임에 참여할 것을 권유하고 있으므로 이 담화의 목적으로 ④ ‘학생들에게 점심시간 걷기 모임에 참여하도록 권장하기 위해’가 적절하다.

body:
W: Logan, how was your weekend? Did you do anything special?
M: It was good. I went to the city homeless shelter as usual.
W: Are you saying that you visit there regularly?
M: Yeah. I volunteer there every Saturday, serving meals to people at the shelter.
W: That’s amazing. It must be rewarding.
M: It really is. Every week, I feel like I’ve made a difference in people’s lives.
W: That’s awesome. Did you know that volunteering can have a positive impact on your health, too?
M: What do you mean? Like an impact on physical health?
W: Yes. It can actually decrease your blood pressure and cholesterol level. It’s called the “Mother Teresa effect.”
M: Interesting... So rather than just helping others when I volunteer, it sounds like I’m benefiting a lot, too.
W: Kindness makes a world of difference!

다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Logan volunteers at a homeless shelter every weekend.
One of the reasons Logan visits the shelter is to improve his physical health.
Volunteering can lower blood pressure and cholesterol levels.
Logan was not aware of the positive health effects of volunteering called the “Mother Teresa effect.”
Logan believes volunteering has made a meaningful difference in people’s lives.
solution:
대화 후반부에 Logan은 여자의 말을 통해 자원봉사가 신체적 건강에 미치는 긍정적인 효과에 대해 알게 되었으므로, ② ‘Logan이 보호소를 방문하는 이유 중 하나는 자신의 신체적 건강을 향상시키기 위해서이다.’는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
오답
① Logan은 매주 주말 노숙인 보호소에서 자원봉사를 한다.
③ 자원봉사는 혈압과 콜레스테롤 수치를 낮출 수 있다.
④ Logan은 ‘마더 테레사 효과’라고 불리는 자원봉사의 긍정적인 건강 효과를 알지 못했다.
⑤ Logan은 자원봉사가 사람들의 삶에 의미 있는 변화를 가져왔다고 생각한다.

body:
A New English Word
After eating a delicious meal, we feel full, happy, and relaxed. That doesn’t occur when we are hungry; hunger causes discomfort and weakness and often (A)sparks negative emotions. “You’re not you when you’re hungry,” was a famous candy bar (B)commercial slogan a few years ago. What this slogan means ⓐto be hunger can seriously change your mood and performance. The (C)phenomenon of getting annoyed and irritated due to hunger is so common ⓑthat the word “hangry,” a combination of hungry and angry, has become an official English word in many international dictionaries. So how does it work?

Hunger and Psychology
The word hangry caught the attention of psychologists, so researchers conducted a series of experiments with over two hundred U.S. college students. Participants were asked to either (D)skip eating or eat a big meal right before the experiment. Their performance and behavior at varying levels of difficulty in tasks involving selective attention, mental rotation, writing, and frustration management were ⓒrecorded and analyzed. The results showed that participants who skipped eating had poorer performance than ⓓthose who ate beforehand. For example, they made more errors on the Stroop task, in which the participants were shown a color name that ⓔwas printed in a different colored ink, and they were asked to say either the word or the color of the ink. Consequently, psychological studies seem to (E)suggest that an empty stomach contributes to lower attention span and self-control.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓐ to be → is (명사절 주어 ‘What this slogan means’에 이어지는 동사 자리이며, 절은 단수 취급하므로 to be를 단수동사 is로 고친다.)
오답
ⓑ 완전한 절(the ~ dictionaries)을 이끌어, 부사 so, 형용사 common와 함께 ‘so+형용사/부사+that+완전한 절(매우 ~해서 …하다)‘의 구문을 이루고 있으므로 접속사 that은 적절하다.
ⓒ 주어 Their performance and behavior가 ’기록된‘ 대상이므로 be동사 were와 함께 쓰여 수동태(be+p.p.)를 이루는 과거분사 recorded는 적절하다.
ⓓ that절의 주어인 복수명사 participants를 가리키므로, 복수 대명사 those는 적절하다.
ⓔ 선행사 a color name을 수식하는 관계사절의 동사 자리로, a color name이 ’출력된‘ 대상이며 과거를 나타내야 하므로 과거형 수동태 was printed는 적절하다.
본문변형 a color name printed → a color name that was printed

solution:

A New English Word
After eating a delicious meal, we feel full, happy, and relaxed. That doesn’t occur when we are hungry; hunger causes discomfort and weakness and often (A)sparks negative emotions. “You’re not you when you’re hungry,” was a famous candy bar (B)commercial slogan a few years ago. What this slogan means ⓐto be hunger can seriously change your mood and performance. The (C)phenomenon of getting annoyed and irritated due to hunger is so common ⓑthat the word “hangry,” a combination of hungry and angry, has become an official English word in many international dictionaries. So how does it work?

Hunger and Psychology
The word hangry caught the attention of psychologists, so researchers conducted a series of experiments with over two hundred U.S. college students. Participants were asked to either (D)skip eating or eat a big meal right before the experiment. Their performance and behavior at varying levels of difficulty in tasks involving selective attention, mental rotation, writing, and frustration management were ⓒrecorded and analyzed. The results showed that participants who skipped eating had poorer performance than ⓓthose who ate beforehand. For example, they made more errors on the Stroop task, in which the participants were shown a color name that ⓔwas printed in a different colored ink, and they were asked to say either the word or the color of the ink. Consequently, psychological studies seem to (E)suggest that an empty stomach contributes to lower attention span and self-control.

choices: Being hungry may leave people feeling and performing quite differently.
Hunger often causes irritation, so “hangry” became an official English word.
Researchers studied the relationship between eating and emotions.
Those without a meal beforehand performed worse on the Stroop task.
An empty stomach can weaken concentration and the ability to control oneself.

body:
Hunger and Hormones
Psychology is not the only field of science concerned with the relation between hunger and anger; physiologists know that hunger leads to changes in body reactions, too. When we eat bread, rice, or fruit, our digestive system breaks these foods down into glucose, the main fuel source for the cells in our body. It circulates in the blood and gets absorbed by cells for the energy required for their proper performance. But glucose levels fall when we are hungry, preventing cells from performing the thing ⓐthat they are supposed to do, an obvious threat to the proper functioning of the body. The human body responds to this threat by ⓑreleasing cortisol, a hormone that helps our body cope with stressful situations. Elevated cortisol levels lead to an increase in heart rate and blood pressure along with many psychological effects including anxiety, irritation, and depression. These physiological reactions seem to be in line with psychological studies.

Hunger and the Brain
What is also affected by an empty stomach is the brain. Neurologists ⓒhave found that high levels of cortisol cause the serotonin level in the brain to drop. Serotonin is a neurotransmitter that helps communication among neurons in different parts of the brain. Neurotransmitters play a crucial role in maintaining emotional balance and an overall sense of well-being. When serotonin levels are not balanced, normal functioning of mood regulation is disrupted, ⓓwhich can lead to feelings of sadness, increased irritability, and higher levels of anxiety. Neurologists have also come across interesting findings related to hunger and mental state by using brain imaging techniques to take pictures of brain activity. These images clearly show that, when people are hungry, areas related to threat and negative emotions increase in activity, while the activity patterns in areas responsible for higher cognitive skills like self-control and decision-making ⓔis greatly altered. Psychology, physiology, and neurology seem to agree that “You’re not you when you’re hungry.”

While being hangry refers to the emotional feelings of anger caused by the physical needs of the body, a phenomenon (A)[called / calling] “lonely hunger” works the other way around, namely from the feelings of loneliness to the need for physical nourishment. That is, some people feel hungry when they feel lonely and (B)[isolating / isolated] from others, often looking for comfort in excessive “emotional eating.” Emotional eating may be a good way to relieve negative emotions in the short term, but it is not necessarily a good long-term solution due to health risks.
Interestingly, the human brain’s response to loneliness is similar to its response to hunger, as brain imaging studies have shown that the same area in the brain is turned on when a person has these feelings. Studies also support the notion (C)[that / what] loneliness serves as a signal similar to hunger, indicating a lack that needs to be addressed. Just as a lack of physical nourishment leads to psychological discomfort, a lack of social nourishment results in feelings of social hunger, a deficit that needs to be addressed.

body:
You Are in Control
Does this mean that everyone who is hungry gets irritated about something? No. (A) Individuals vary in their genes and personality as well as in their lifestyle and experiences, so their physiological or neurological reactions to hunger can vary as well. (B) In fact, scientists have observed that the behavior of many animals is closely linked to the availability of nourishment, too. (C) For example, fruit flies get more aggressive when deprived of food, and schooling fish exhibit reduced group unity when hungry. (D) Some researchers are also interested in how eating habits can influence people’s daily energy levels. (E) Regardless, there is another interesting finding from the research of psychologists on hunger: People seem to be able to control their negative emotions, but only if they are able to recognize them. If you happen to find yourself angry, take a few deep breaths and ask yourself if you skipped lunch. What might be happening is you’re just hangry.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E) 중, 흐름상 관계없는 문장은?
solution: 배고픔이 감정(짜증, 분노 등)과 생리·신경학적 반응에 미치는 영향, 그리고 이를 인지하고 조절하는 방법이 글의 핵심 내용이다. (A)에서는 배고픔에 대한 사람들의 생리적·신경학적 반응이 개인마다 다를 수 있다고 설명하고, (B)와 (C)에서는 이러한 배고픔과 동물의 행동 사이의 관계를 구체적인 사례를 통해 보여 주며, (E)에서는 배고픔으로 인한 부정적 감정을 인식하고 조절하는 방법에 관한 내용으로 자연스럽게 이어진다. 그러나 (D) ‘일부 연구자들은 식습관이 사람들의 일상적인 에너지 수준에 어떻게 영향을 미칠 수 있는지에도 관심을 가지고 있다.’는 배고픔에 따른 행동 변화 및 부정적 감정을 인식하고 조절하는 방법과는 관련이 없으므로 (D)가 글의 흐름과 관계없다.

Some people seem to have a deep dislike of certain foods like cucumbers. Did you know that this may be due to genetics rather than preference? Cucumbers and other similar plants produce a bitter substance around the stem, which seems to protect the plant against bugs and animals. Researchers have discovered that there is a particular gene that makes some people very sensitive to the taste of bitterness, while others are less bothered by it. Moreover, other foods like watermelon, sweet melon, or even cilantro might get the thumbs down from people sensitive to the gene, too! So you can blame your genes if you don’t like those foods.
But wait, there’s more! Some individuals have an issue with the smell of cucumbers in addition to the bitter taste. Genes influence the way we smell things in general, and some people are sensitive to chemical compounds that are key to the cucumber smell. ⓐ우리의 후각은 우리 각자만큼이나 독특하며, 400가지가 넘는 종류의 후각 수용체로 다양성을 만들어 낸다. While scientists are currently searching for the precise receptors linked to the cucumber scent, some genes might make certain individuals more sensitive to those compounds. For example, some people may detect a soap- or lotion-like scent from cilantro due to the chemical compounds it contains.
We all seem to be wired differently when it comes to taste preferences. More than just a matter of whether you like or dislike something, it could come from something deep within our DNA. Thus, maybe it’s not appropriate to give people a hard time for disliking certain foods. Let’s celebrate the fact that we are all different and share a plate of understanding.

Neurologists have also come across interesting findings related to hunger and mental state by using brain imaging techniques to take pictures of brain activity. body:
Loneliness and Hunger
While being hangry refers to the emotional feelings of anger caused by the physical needs of the body, a phenomenon called “lonely hunger” works the other way around, namely from the feelings of loneliness to the need for physical nourishment. That is, some people feel hungry when they ______, often looking for comfort in excessive “emotional eating.” Emotional eating may be a good way to relieve negative emotions in the short term, but it is not necessarily a good long-term solution due to health risks.
Interestingly, the human brain’s response to loneliness is similar to its response to hunger, as brain imaging studies have shown that the same area in the brain is turned on when a person has these feelings. Studies also support the notion that loneliness serves as a signal similar to hunger, indicating a lack that needs to be addressed. Just as a lack of physical nourishment leads to psychological discomfort, a lack of social nourishment results in feelings of social hunger, a deficit that needs to be addressed.

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: feel socially disconnected and emotionally isolated
experience sudden drops in blood glucose levels
go through prolonged periods of physical exhaustion
fail to manage emotional stress through long-term solutions
develop stronger emotional connections through social interaction
solution:
문장의 맨 앞에 연결어 That is(다시 말해서)가 사용되었으므로, 빈칸을 포함한 문장은 앞 문장의 내용을 구체적으로 다시 설명하는 역할을 한다. 앞 문장에서 ‘외로움에서 오는 허기’가 외로움이라는 감정에서 신체적 영양분에 대한 욕구로 이어지는 현상이라고 설명했으므로, 외로움을 느끼고 다른 사람들과 단절되었을 때 배고픔을 느낀다는 내용이 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다. 따라서 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 ① ‘사회적으로 단절되고 정서적으로 고립되어 있다고 느끼다’가 적절하다.
본문변형 feel lonely and isolated from others → feel socially disconnected and emotionally isolated
오답
② 혈당 수치가 갑자기 떨어지는 것을 경험하다
③ 장기간의 신체적 피로를 겪다
④ 장기적인 해결책을 통해 정서적 스트레스를 관리하지 못하다
⑤ 사회적 상호작용을 통해 더 강한 정서적 유대감을 형성하다

M: Hey, Kate! You seem a bit down.
W: Ugh, I made a big mistake during my presentation. I can’t stop thinking about it.
M: Oh, that’s tough. But hey, how about going outside and soaking up some sunlight?
W: Hmm, I don’t think that’ll change my mood.
M: Trust me! Sunlight stimulates the production of vitamin D, (A)[which / what] plays a crucial role in serotonin production. This natural boost in serotonin levels can have significant effects on your mood.
W: I’m not sure I understand. Are you saying (B)[what / that] sunlight can actually improve my mood?
M: Exactly! Look at this article I read. It says sunlight triggers the release of serotonin, which (C)[calls / is called] the “feel-good” hormone.
W: Alright, I’ll give it a try.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: which / that / calls
what / what / is called
which / that / is called
what / what / calls
which / what / is called
solution:
(A) 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(plays ~ production)을 이끌어 콤마(,) 앞의 선행사 vitamin D를 부연 설명하는 계속적 용법의 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which가 적절하다.
(B) 완전한 절(sunlight ~ mood)을 이끌어 saying의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 명사절 접속사 that이 적절하다.
(C) 콤마(,) 앞의 선행사 serotonin을 부연 설명하는 관계사절의 동사 자리이며, serotonin이 "기분 좋은" 호르몬이라고 ‘불리는’ 대상이므로 수동태 is called가 적절하다.

body:
Jenny was up late last night finishing an assignment after her part-time job. She had to skip breakfast this morning in a rush to catch the bus for school. By doing so, she made matters worse because she has to sit through and focus on her difficult science class. As the class drags on, her hunger builds, and she starts tapping her pencil on her desk and shooting angry glances at the clock. Her classmates start noticing her mood, and some are even laughing at her stomach noises. Embarrassed and angry, she snaps at her friends. Have you ever felt like Jenny?

A New English Word
After eating a delicious meal, we feel full, happy, and relaxed. That doesn’t occur when we are hungry; hunger causes discomfort and weakness and often sparks negative emotions. “You’re not you when you’re hungry,” was a famous candy bar commercial slogan a few years ago. What this slogan means is hunger can seriously change your mood and performance. The phenomenon of getting annoyed and irritated due to hunger is so common that the word “hangry,” a combination of hungry and angry, has become an official English word in many international dictionaries. So how does it work?

다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?
choices: Why did Jenny have to skip breakfast in the morning?
How did Jenny behave as she became hungrier during her science class?
Why does a delicious meal make us feel happy and relaxed?
What does the slogan “You’re not you when you’re hungry” mean?
What words were combined to create the official English word “hangry”?

body:
Hunger and Psychology
The word hangry caught the attention of psychologists, so researchers conducted a series of experiments with over two hundred U.S. college students. Participants were asked to either ⓐskip eating or eat a big meal right before the experiment. Their performance and behavior at varying levels of difficulty in tasks involving selective attention, mental rotation, writing, and frustration management were recorded and ⓑanalyzed. The results showed that participants who skipped eating ⓒhad poorer performance than those who ate beforehand. For example, they made more errors on the Stroop task, in which the participants were ⓓshowing a color name printed in a different colored ink, and they ⓔwere asked to say either the word or the color of the ink. Consequently, psychological studies seem to suggest (A)______.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓓ showing → shown (주어 the participants가 색 이름이 ‘보여진’ 대상이므로 앞의 be동사 were과 함께 수동태를 이루도록 showing을 과거분사 shown으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ ‘~하기를 요청받다’를 뜻하는 ‘be asked+to부정사’의 구조로, 앞의 to와 함께 to부정사를 이루는 동사원형 skip은 적절하다.
ⓑ 주어 Their performance and behavior가 기록되고 분석되는 대상이므로 등위접속사 and 앞에 있는 be동사 were와 함께 쓰여 수동태(be+p.p.)를 이루는 과거분사 analyzed는 적절하다.
ⓒ that절의 주어 participants를 선행사로 수식하는 관계사절(who skipped eating) 뒤에 이어지는 동사 자리이며, 실험이 과거에 발생했으므로 과거형 동사 had는 적절하다.
ⓔ 주어 they(=the participants)가 말하도록 ‘요청 받은’ 대상이므로 수동태 were asked는 적절하다.

body:
Psychology is not the only field of science concerned with the relation between hunger and anger; physiologists know that hunger leads to changes in ⓐbody reactions, too. When we eat bread, rice, or fruit, our digestive system breaks these foods down into glucose, the main fuel source for the cells in our body. It circulates in the blood and gets absorbed by cells for the energy (A)[requiring / required] for their proper performance. But glucose levels ⓑfall when we are hungry, (B)[prevent / preventing] cells from performing what they are supposed to do, an obvious ⓒhazard to the proper functioning of the body. The human body responds to this threat by releasing cortisol, a hormone that helps our body (C)[cope / coping] with stressful situations. ⓓReduced cortisol levels lead to an increase in heart rate and blood pressure along with many psychological effects including anxiety, irritation, and depression. These ⓔphysiological reactions seem to be in line with psychological studies.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 흐름상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓓ Reduced (줄어든) → Elevated (높아진)
본문변형 ⓒ threat → hazard

body:
Does this mean that everyone who is hungry gets irritated about something? No. Individuals vary in their genes and personality as well as in their lifestyle and experiences, so their physiological or neurological reactions to hunger can vary as well. In fact, scientists have observed that the behavior of many animals is closely linked to the availability of nourishment, too. For example, fruit flies get more aggressive when deprived of food, and schooling fish exhibit reduced group unity when hungry. Regardless, there is another interesting finding from the research of psychologists on hunger: People seem to be able to control their negative emotions, but only if they are able to recognize them. If you happen to find yourself angry, take a few deep breaths and ask yourself if you skipped lunch. What might be happening is you’re just hangry.

다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Individual variations in genes, personality, and experiences lead to different responses to hunger.
An animal's behavior can be influenced by whether it has access to enough food.
When deprived of food, fruit flies become more aggressive, while schooling fish show stronger group unity.
Recognizing negative emotions allows people to manage them more successfully.
To check if you skipped a meal can help you realize that your sudden anger is simply due to being hangry.

body:
While being hangry refers to the emotional feelings of anger caused by the physical needs of the body, a phenomenon called “lonely hunger” works the other way around, namely from the feelings of loneliness to the need for physical nourishment. That is, some people feel hungry when they feel lonely and isolated from others, often looking for comfort in excessive “emotional eating.” Emotional eating may be a good way to relieve negative emotions in the short term, but it is not necessarily a good long-term solution due to health risks.
Interestingly, the human brain’s response to loneliness is similar to its response to hunger, as brain imaging studies have shown that the same area in the brain is turned on when a person has these feelings. Studies also support the notion that loneliness serves as a signal similar to hunger, indicating a lack that needs to be addressed. Just as a lack of physical nourishment leads to psychological discomfort, a lack of social nourishment results in feelings of social hunger, a deficit that needs to be addressed.

윗글의 내용과 (A)~(D)가 일치하면 T, 일치하지 않으면 F를 쓸 때, 순서대로 연결된 것은?
(A) “Lonely hunger” refers to a phenomenon where physical hunger causes a person to feel socially isolated. (T/F)
(B) Brain imaging shows that different brain areas are activated by loneliness and physical hunger. (T/F)
(C) Emotional eating can temporarily ease negative emotions, but it can pose long-term health risks. (T/F)
(D) While a lack of physical nourishment leads to psychological discomfort, a lack of social nourishment causes social hunger. (T/F)
choices: F-T-T-T
F-F-T-T
T-F-F-T
T-T-F-F
F-F-F-T
solution:

(A) ‘외로움에서 오는 허기’는 신체적인 배고픔이 사람으로 하여금 사회적으로 고립되었다고 느끼게 하는(→외로움이라는 감정에서 신체적 영양분에 대한 욕구로 이어지는) 현상을 의미한다. (불일치)
(B) 뇌 영상은 외로움과 신체적인 배고픔에 의해 서로 다른(→동일한) 뇌 영역이 활성화된다는 것을 보여 준다. (불일치)
(C) 감정적 섭식은 부정적인 감정을 일시적으로 완화할 수 있지만, 장기적인 건강 위험을 초래할 수 있다. (일치)

body:
The human body responds to this threat by releasing cortisol, a hormone that helps our body cope with stressful situations.

Hunger and Hormones
Psychology is not the only field of science concerned with the relation between hunger and anger; physiologists know that hunger leads to changes in body reactions, too. (A) When we eat bread, rice, or fruit, our digestive system breaks these foods down into glucose, the main fuel source for the cells in our body. (B) It circulates in the blood and gets absorbed by cells for the energy required for their proper performance. (C) But glucose levels fall when we are hungry, preventing cells from performing what they are supposed to do, an obvious threat to the proper functioning of the body. (D) Elevated cortisol levels lead to an increase in heart rate and blood pressure along with many psychological effects including anxiety, irritation, and depression. (E) These physiological reactions seem to be in line with psychological studies.

다음 글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘인체는 코르티솔을 분비함으로써 이러한 위협에 대응하는데, 이는 우리 신체가 스트레스 상황에 대처하는 데 도움을 주는 호르몬이다.’라는 뜻으로, 이 문장 앞에는 this threat으로 가리킬 수 있는 인체에 위협이 되는 상황이 제시되어야 한다. 따라서 (D) 앞에서 배가 고프면 포도당 수치는 떨어지고, 세포가 해야 하는 일을 수행하지 못하게 되며, 이것이 신체의 정상적인 기능에 위협이 된다고 했는데, 여기서 언급된 위협(an obvious threat)이 주어진 문장에서 this threat로 이어지며, 그 위협에 대응하기 위해 코르티솔(cortisol)이 분비된다고 설명하는데 이것이 (D) 뒤에서 Elevated cortisol levels(높아진 코르티솔 수치)로 이어지므로, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 적절한 곳은 (D)이다.

body:
Some people seem to have a deep dislike of certain foods like cucumbers. Did you know that this may be due to genetics rather than preference? Cucumbers and other similar plants produce a bitter substance around the stem, which ⓐseem to protect the plant against bugs and animals. Researchers have discovered ⓑthat there is a particular gene that makes some people very sensitive to the taste of bitterness, while others are less bothered by it. Moreover, other foods like watermelon, sweet melon, or even cilantro might get the thumbs down from people sensitive to the gene, too! So you can blame your genes if you don’t like those foods.
But wait, there’s more! Some individuals have an issue with the smell of cucumbers in addition to the bitter taste. Genes influence the way we smell things in general, and some people are sensitive to chemical compounds that are key to the cucumber smell. Our sense of smell is as unique as we are, with over 400 types of smell receptors, ⓒcreating plentiful variations. While scientists are currently searching for the precise receptors linked to the cucumber scent, some genes might make certain individuals more sensitive to those compounds. For example, some people may detect a soap- or lotion-like scent from cilantro due to the chemical compounds it contains.
We all seem to be wired differently when it comes to taste preferences. More than just a matter of whether you like or dislike something, it could come from something deep within our DNA. Thus, maybe it’s not appropriate ⓓto give people a hard time for disliking certain foods. Let’s celebrate the fact ⓔwhich we are all different and share a plate of understanding.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the unique substances found in foods like cucumbers and their characteristics
ways to overcome the tendency to avoid foods with unpleasant tastes and smells
individual variations in food taste and smell preferences caused by genetics
how environmental factors and personal habits shape our food preferences
chemical compounds that help protect plants from animals and insects

body:
You Are in Control
Does this mean that everyone who is hungry gets (A)[irritated / irritating] about something? No. Individuals vary in their genes and personality as well as in their lifestyle and experiences, so their physiological or neurological reactions to hunger can vary as well. In fact, scientists have observed that the behavior of many animals is closely linked to the availability of nourishment, too. For example, fruit flies get more aggressive when deprived of food, and schooling fish exhibit reduced group unity when hungry. Regardless, there is another interesting finding from the research of psychologists on hunger: People seem to be able to control their negative emotions, but only if they are able to recognize them. If you happen to find yourself angry, take a few deep breaths and ask yourself (B)[what / if] you skipped lunch. (C)[That / What] might be happening is you’re just hangry.

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: irritating / what / That
irritated / if / That
irritated / what / What
irritating / what / What
irritated / if / What
solution:
(A) 2형식으로 쓰인 동사 gets의 보어 자리로, 주어 everyone who is hungry가 ‘짜증 난’ 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 irritated가 적절하다.
(B) ‘ask+간접목적어+직접목적어‘의 4형식 동사 ask의 직접목적어 역할을 하는 완전한 절(you ~ lunch)을 이끌어 ’~인지 아닌지‘의 의미를 갖는 명사절 접속사 if가 적절하다.
(C) ‘~하는 것’이라는 뜻으로 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(might be happening)을 이끌어 문장의 주어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 What이 적절하다.

body:
Hunger and Psychology
The word hangry caught the attention of psychologists, so researchers conducted a series of experiments with over two hundred U.S. college students. Participants were asked to either skip eating or eat a big meal right before the experiment. Their performance and behavior at varying levels of difficulty in tasks ⓐinvolve selective attention, mental rotation, writing, and frustration management were recorded and analyzed. The results showed that participants who skipped eating had (A)______ than those who ate beforehand. For example, they made more errors on the Stroop task, ⓑwhich the participants were shown a color name printed in a different colored ink, and they were asked to say either the word or the color of the ink. Consequently, psychological studies seem to suggest that an empty stomach contributes to lower attention span and self-control.

Hunger and the Brain
What is also affected by an empty stomach is the brain. ㉠신경학자들은 코르티솔의 높은 수치는 뇌 속의 세로토닌 수치가 감소시킨다는 것을 밝혀냈다. Serotonin is a neurotransmitter that ⓒhelps communication among neurons in different parts of the brain. Neurotransmitters play a crucial role in maintaining emotional balance and an overall sense of well-being. When serotonin levels are not balanced, normal functioning of (B)______ is disturbed, which can lead to feelings of sadness, increased irritability, and higher levels of anxiety. Neurologists have also come across interesting findings related to hunger and mental state by ⓓusing brain imaging techniques to take pictures of brain activity. These images clearly show that, when people are hungry, areas related to threat and negative emotions increase in activity, while the activity patterns in areas responsible for higher cognitive skills like self-control and decision-making ⓔare greatly altered. Psychology, physiology, and neurology seem to agree that “You’re not you when you’re hungry.”

윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B)
choices: worse outcomes / digestive processes
better memory / emotional control
greater accuracy / long-term memory
poorer performance / mood regulation
higher physical energy / glucose absorption
solution:
(A) 뒤에 이어지는 예시인 스트룹(Stroop) 과제에서 식사를 거른 참가자들이 실수를 더 많이 했다고 언급되고 있으며, 마지막 문장에서 심리학 연구들은 공복 상태가 더 낮은 주의 지속 시간과 자기 통제력에 일조한다는 점을 뒷받침한다고 언급하고 있으므로, 식사를 거른 참가자들이 '더 나쁜 결과들(worse outcomes)' 또는 ‘더 낮은 수행능력(poorer performance)’을 가졌다는 흐름이 자연스럽다.
*본문에는 poorer performance가 쓰였음
(B) 앞 문장에서 신경 전달 물질인 세로토닌이 감정의 균형 및 전반적인 안정감을 유지하는 데 중요한 역할을 한다고 했으므로, 세로토닌 수치가 불균형해지면 방해 받게 되는 정상적인 기능으로 ‘감정 조절(emotional control, mood regulation)’이 빈칸에 들어가는 것이 자연스럽다.
*본문에는 mood regulation이 쓰였음
